sections.Notes:
* Magdalene's strength lies in her naturally high health and her starting item, {{I|Yum Heart}}.
** With her high number of Red Heart containers, Magdalene can afford more {{R|Devil Room}} deals.
** She has more health to spend on sacrifices, including {{e|Blood Donation Machine}}s, {{R|Sacrifice Room}}s, and items that grant effects upon taking damage like {{I|Bloody Lust}}.
** {{dlc|r}} In [[Repentance Co-Op|co-op]], {{I|Yum Heart}} will also heal other players for half a Red Heart when used.
** {{dlc|r}} If Magdalene is at full health, combined with a fully charged {{I|Yum Heart}} and a Full Health pill, she can step on a {{R|Sacrifice Room}} spike seven times, allowing her to potentially get two {{R|Angel Room}} items on the first floor. However, this will leave her with only a single Red Heart. Many Angel items are defensive in nature, which will often mitigate this.
* Magdalene's biggest weakness is her low starting speed. Obtaining items that increase speed should be prioritized, as she may not be able to dodge high-speed or homing attacks.
** {{dlc|a+nr}} Once the Aprils Fool challenge is completed, this disadvantage is removed as she will start every run with a Speed Up pill.

sections.Notes:
* While playing as Tainted ???, bomb pickups are replaced by poop pickups, and his bomb counter is replaced by a poop counter which displays the number and effects of his poops. The order in which different types of poop are obtained is predetermined based on the seed. By default, Tainted ??? can carry a maximum of 10 poops: 9 in the poop counter and 1 in Hold.
* Using Hold will store his leftmost poop for later use and cycle to the next poop.
* Besides replacing bomb pickups, poop pickups also have a chance to drop from fallen enemies and from Tainted ??? by dealing damage. There are small and large variants of poop pickups: small poop pickups give one poop, and large poop pickups give three poops.
* Most items that affect bomb count will spawn blue flies when playing as Tainted ???. For example, {{P|2 of Clubs}} and {{i|Boom!}} will spawn 2 and 10 flies, respectively.
** {{dlc|nr+}} However, [[Bombs Are Key]] pills seem to give Tainted ??? bombs internally (assuming he had keys before using the pill), as using the pill again will give back the amount of keys that were originally carried. When bombs are obtained this way, they can be given to {{e|Bomb Bum}}s, though the number of bombs is invisible.
* Items/effects that reroll pickups (such as {{i|D20}}, {{i|GB Bug}}, etc.) will also reroll poop pickups.
** {{p|IX - The Hermit?}} will not convert poop pickups into coins.
* Tainted ???'s poops cannot be used to bridge over gaps, unlike the poops from {{i|The Poop}}.
* In Co-Op, partners can pick up poop drops if they're alive and still add them to Tainted ???'s reserve.
* In Co-Op, a bomb counter will be displayed if one of the characters is not Tainted ???, despite him not usually being able to see it.
* In Co-Op, Tainted ??? can infinitely use Bomb Bums without taking away bombs from the other player's reserves.
* Tainted ??? is unable to give poop pickups to Bomb Bums in place of bombs.
* Tainted ???'s tears are colored brown; this is purely cosmetic.
sections.Strategy:
* As Tainted ??? begins with a low tears stat, it is almost required to rely on poops in the early game. The player should not be scared to use poops, as Tainted ??? will naturally create many poops as he deals damage, especially in boss battles. However, it may be best to save more powerful poops or poop synergies, such as White Poops and brown creep, for more difficult situations such as boss battles.
** Tainted ???'s low tears also makes tears up items like {{I|Torn Photo}} very beneficial.
* More than any other type of poop, it can be beneficial to use Hold on bomb poops for utility purposes, such as finding {{r|Secret Room}}s or reaching pickups behind rocks.
** Alternatively, flaming poops can be used in conjunction with stinky poops/farts to blow things up without using bombs. The stinky poop/fart can be used next to what the player wants to blow up, then the flaming poop can be thrown at it to create an explosion. This can also be done by throwing stinky poops at a fire or flaming poop, though care must be taken as it is easy to get caught in the ensuing explosion if the player does not move out of the way quickly enough.
* If playing in [[Greed Mode]], it's best to try to complete all waves in one sitting as exiting the main room will cause all poops and creep to disappear.
* '''Almost anything''' that resembles a fire can cause toxic clouds created by farts and Stinky Poop to explode. This includes {{e|Fire Place}}s, fires shot by enemies (such as {{E|Candler}}s, {{E|Fire Worm}}s, and {{E|Revenant}}s), and fires created by Tainted ??? (such as with {{i|The Candle}}, {{I|Ghost Pepper}}, and {{I|Bird's Eye}}). Extra caution must be taken to stay away from gas clouds if playing with or around fires.
** {{I|Urn of Souls}} is a notable exception to this.
** Stinky Poops can intentionally be thrown at blue/purple fireplaces to blow them up for the chance to gain {{e|Soul Heart}}s. Be careful not to destroy [[Angel|Angel statues]] next to them if they’re in an {{R|Angel Room}} if you do not wish to fight the angel.

* Due to Samson's starting item, {{i|Bloody Lust}}, he has a playstyle that is similar to {{C|Eve}}. Therefore, health sacrifices such as {{e|Devil Beggar}}s, {{R|Sacrifice Room}}s, and {{e|Blood Donation Machine}}s are recommended.
** As a result, anything that lowers health is not recommended, as that will make self-damage less effective. {{R|Angel Room}}s are more valuable than {{R|Devil Room}}s, if the player comes across any.
* {{dlc|nr}} The first three times Samson is hit, his damage is increased by 0.5. The next three times Samson is hit, his damage is increased by 33%.
* {{dlc|r}} Damage is increased by flat amounts: +0.5 for the first hit and an additional +0.2 for each hit, until +1.5 at the sixth. This means that the maximum total is +6.0.
* Samson's starting trinket, {{t|Child's Heart}}, is one of the more optional unlocks — the trinket itself is not too powerful, not to mention it requiring the completion of the [[Ultra Hard]] challenge.
* When Samson dies in [[co-op]], his ghost baby maintains his level of rage from Bloody Lust, giving it a red tint. This is purely visual.
* Dying as Samson and then respawning as another character (with {{i|Lazarus' Rags}}, {{i|Ankh}}, etc.) will make them inherit Samson's {{i|Bloody Lust}} item.

'''Tainted Forgotten''' and '''Tainted Soul''' are [[Characters]] added in [[The Binding of Isaac: Repentance]]. They are the tainted versions of {{c|The Forgotten}} and {{c|The Soul}}. Tainted Forgotten is unlocked by reaching {{s|Home}} and using the {{I|Red Key}}, {{P|Cracked Key}}, or {{P|1=Soul of Cain}} to access a special room in the left hallway while playing as The Forgotten.

sections.Notes:
* Both characters always co-exist and depend on each other; Tainted Soul is incapable of firing tears or dealing damage in almost any manner, and likewise, Tainted Forgotten is incapable of moving on their own. Tainted Soul is able to pick up and move around with, or throw, Tainted Forgotten, similar to how one holds and throws {{i|Bob's Rotten Head}}. Otherwise, Tainted Forgotten has a melee bone weapon like {{c|The Forgotten}} does, which he can swing and throw while on the ground.
** Tainted Forgotten will swing his bone at the same time Tainted Soul throws him, and this swing will deal 3x the normal damage, and the impact itself will deal 5 damage.
* Tainted Forgotten is also completely invulnerable, and instead, Tainted Soul acts as his 'hitbox' and will take damage like any character. Both characters share the same pool of {{e|Soul Heart}}s (they cannot have {{e|Red Heart}} Containers), and if the last one is lost, they both die.
* Enemies almost always target Tainted Soul and ignore Tainted Forgotten, but the latter's body can be used to block enemy projectiles and movement.
* Both share the same pool of pickups, similar to {{c|The Forgotten}}. Tainted Forgotten can pick up items and consumables when he's thrown at them, as well as open Chests or unlock doors.
* Tainted Forgotten can be thrown into a door to enter the next room (including {{r|Curse Room}}s, which deal no damage to Tainted Forgotten), and after entering a room, Tainted Soul will always be holding him. With practice, they can very rapidly traverse the floor, spending a fraction of a second in any cleared room.
* When placing a {{e|Bomb}}, it will be placed underneath Tainted Forgotten, and the same is true when dropping trinkets or Cards, etc.
* Any items picked up will normally behave as if Tainted Forgotten picked them up and don't directly affect Tainted Soul; for example, orbital [[familiars]] will orbit Tainted Forgotten. Speed upgrades on the other hand will apply to Tainted Soul, among other examples. Effects that grant invincibility, i.e. {{i|Book of Shadows}}, will apply to Tainted Soul, whether or not there's visual indication of this.
* Tainted Soul can open the door to {{s|Mausoleum}} / {{s|Gehenna}} without losing any health while not holding Tainted Forgotten.
* If Tainted Soul picks up Tainted Forgotten while the latter is charging a bone toss, it will throw it once the player releases the attack button.
* If Tainted Forgotten's range reaches high enough numbers, his melee bone swing will occur away from him, which can result in an inability to deal damage to enemies too close to him.
* {{E|Bulb}}s will never attack both Tainted Forgotten or Tainted Soul.
sections.Strategy:
* In order to one-throw-kill as many enemies as possible, Tainted Forgotten's build should focus on [[Damage]]. Having high [[Speed]] is also important, as it allows Tainted Soul to pick Tainted Forgotten up easier. [[Tears]] and [[Range]] are less useful than normal for Tainted Forgotten.
* Items that enhance melee attack radius (such as size-up items, {{i|Chocolate Milk}}, {{i|Mutant Spider}}, {{i|Technology}}) are also recommended. Items that split tears on hit like {{i|Haemolacria}} are beneficial as well.
* Items with area of effect damage such as {{i|Monstrance}} and {{i|120 Volt}} apply their effect to Tainted Forgotten, making them incredibly powerful for large crowds and stationary bosses.
* Care should be taken when fighting enemies spawned in {{r|Devil Room}}s, {{r|Shop}}s and {{r|Black Market}}s, as Tainted Forgotten will buy anything he's thrown into if possible, with potentially fatal results.
* Some [[pills]] don't work or are irrelevant because they apply their effects to Tainted Forgotten. Paralysis is one example.
* Be careful of {{e|Mom's Hand}}s, because they can grab Tainted Forgotten. This will deal no damage, but will still teleport Tainted Forgotten back to the starting room.
* Tainted Soul can open {{E|Mimic Chest}}s without taking damage.
* Tainted Soul can activate the stop button in [[Greed Mode]] without taking damage, at the price of one less coin spawning in the next wave's reward. Tainted Forgotten's body can also be used to activate the button, which does not cost a coin.
* Tainted Soul can pass through the mirror in {{s|Downpour}} / {{s|Dross}} II without touching the {{E|White Fire Place}} (in fact, nothing happens when he flies over it), and will keep his life bar, which makes the trek considerably safer.
** If Tainted Forgotten is thrown into the White Fire Place, he transforms into {{c|The Lost}} (though he is still invulnerable); Tainted Soul will have {{i|Holy Mantle}} protection (if unlocked), but will die if damage is taken after it's broken like normal.
* Items that inflict Fear like {{i|Mom's Perfume}} and {{i|2Spooky}} should be avoided because enemies will flee from Tainted Forgotten instead of Tainted Soul, making it harder to hit enemies while also offering Tainted Soul little protection.
* [[Status Effects#Charm|Charmed]] enemies may pursue Tainted Forgotten instead of other enemies, which can be ideal for bringing and keeping them within range of his melee attack.
* [[Tear Effects|Tear effects]] from items such as {{i|Euthanasia}} and {{i|Sulfuric Acid}} will activate on both body throws and melee attacks.
* All contact damage attacks such as {{i|Aries}} and {{i|The Virus}} are tripled in strength and will apply when throwing Tainted Forgotten. The damage is added on top of the normal 5 points his body impact does. Tainted Soul however does not benefit from them at all.

sections.Notes: * Tainted Isaac can only hold 8 passive items at a time. Tainted Isaac's current 8 passive items are visible in the top-left corner of the screen, with one highlighted by a white square. Upon picking up a 9th passive item, the item currently selected, or rather the item currently in the white square, will be dropped on a pedestal in front of Tainted Isaac. The swap key can be pressed to cycle which item is selected. * In exchange for this, all rerollable item pedestals, {{ip|Shop|text=Shop items}}, and {{ip|Devil Room|text=Devil deals}} will cycle between two items for the player to choose from, essentially a stronger version of {{i|More Options}} + {{i|There's Options}}. Whichever item is currently visible when the item is picked up will be the one selected. Once an item has been picked up it will no longer cycle between items. * {{i|The Polaroid}}, {{i|The Negative}}, {{i|Key Piece 1}}, {{i|Key Piece 2}}, {{i|Knife Piece 1}}, {{i|Knife Piece 2}}, {{i|Dad's Note}}, {{i|Birthright}}, the passive item created when {{I|Damocles}} is used (the one with item ID 656), and all activated items are exempt from this limit and do not take up inventory space. Swallowed [[trinkets]] also do not count towards the 8 item limit. * Dropping items causes their passive buffs to be removed, however health or pickups will be kept (such as from{{i|Breakfast}} or {{i|Pageant Boy}}). Note that pickups will be kept regardless of which way they were gained (picked up or directly added to the counters). * Even if one of the item is a [[Item Pool#Set Drops|set drop]], the other one is still randomly pulled from the current room's item pool.
sections.Strategy:
* While most passive items have their effects "bound" to them, with the changes reverted with the loss of the item, some passive items have a permanent effect that triggers on pickup. HP upgrades like {{I|Breakfast}}, and pickup spawners like {{I|Pageant Boy}} can all be left behind immediately. Many items not having their effects reverted are listed in Synergies and Interactions section.
** Rerolled health items makes Tainted Isaac lose the health "bound". Using the {{I|D4}} or {{I|D100}} or {{I|D infinity}} to reroll passive items then dropping gained health items makes it easier for him to accumulate more health containers.
* Stat changes from [[Pills]] are permanent. This can make them either extremely useful or dangerous, as high natural stats mean less need to carry stat up items, but Tainted Isaac cannot counteract stat downs with items as easily due to the limited inventory.
* Due to the limited amount of items, [[Trinkets]] have a more important role with this character. Therefore any item helping to gain some, such as {{I|Mom's Box}}, will help a lot. Items or pickups that allow to absorb them ({{I|Marbles}}, {{I|Smelter}}, [[Gulp!]]...) are even more important as absorbed trinkets do not take up an item slot.
* [[Transformations]] are permanent, and the progress towards transformations by passive items remains if it is replaced with a new item.
** Transformation progress of an item ''will be lost'' if the passive item is removed in any other way, such as being rerolled with{{I|D4}}, or destroyed by {{I|Sacrificial Altar}}
* Items that would add items directly to Tainted Isaac (such as {{I|Cambion Conception}}, {{I|Monster Manual}}, etc) or pickups that would do the same (such as {{P|Soul of Lilith}}) do not take up an inventory slot.
** If {{p|Soul of Lilith}} is used while Tainted Isaac has an empty slot, the familiar granted by the soul ''will'' take up the slot and can be dropped in exchange for another item as normal.
* On item choice, instead of building up stats, it's more effective to find and optimize strong synergies.
* In Co-op mode, the other character can pick up the items that Tainted Isaac drops but this item will no longer contribute to the transformation it is a part of.
** Killing the Boss of a floor in Co-op mode will spawn a Boss item that cycles between two different options, but any subsequent options will not come with an extra choice.
* Cards like {{P|XIV - Temperance}} or {{P|XX - Judgement}} can be extremely powerful, as they allow to spawn an item from a specific item pool. For example, donating to a Blood Donation Machine will spawn either {{I|Blood Bag}} or {{I|IV Bag}} and cycle with a second item pulled from the current room item pool. This can be used to get powerful items from Angel / Devil Room, or help in completing the collection page if the player wishes to avoid a full game break (such as using {{C|Tainted Cain}} or {{I|D20}}) and is actively looking for items in a specific pool.
* Similar to the above, {{P|VI - The Lovers?}}, {{P|VIII - Justice?}} and {{P|XVII - The Stars?}} allow the generation of items from a specific pool, directly through {{P|VI - The Lovers?}} and {{P|XVII - The Stars?}}, and indirectly through the golden chests spawned by {{P|VIII - Justice?}} if they happen to contain items.
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|Abyss}} / {{i|Void}}: are extremely powerful with Tainted Isaac. Any item left behind (especially health ups and items that give one-time effects such as {{i|Booster Pack}}) can be consumed for stat upgrades or red attack locusts.
* {{i|Birthright}}: Gives Tainted Isaac four more item slots without taking up an item slot itself.
** Birthright can be rerolled by items such as the {{I|D4}}, but it will only partially undo the effect of Birthright. If you had more than 8 items at the time of reroll, the extra items are retained above the usual limit. These extra items do take full effect, and can be rerolled, but are not displayed and cannot be selected to drop next in the set of items.  Collecting Birthright again will show these extra items.
** If Tainted Isaac collects multiple Birthrights (whether by using {{I|Death Certificate}}, {{I|Diplopia}}, {{I|Crooked Penny}}, or any other means) the effect does NOT stack and Isaac receives no additional item slots.
* {{I|Brittle Bones}} / {{i|Candy Heart|nr+}} / {{i|Soul Locket|nr+}} / {{i|Death's List}} / {{I|Consolation Prize}} / {{I|Experimental Treatment}} / {{I|Redemption}}: The stat upgrade(s) will not be reverted when left behind.
* {{I|Eden's Blessing}}: Grants a random item at the start of your next run, even if you are to drop it and not finish your run with it.
* {{i|Lemegeton}}: Each spawned wisp grants a passive item effect which won't count towards an inventory slot. The wisps can be destroyed, losing the corresponding passive effect. Protective items or battery items help maintain wisps throughout a run.
* {{I|Lost Soul}}: Respawns after being hit if swapped for another item and picked back up again, virtually guaranteeing rewards as long as Isaac's inventory is full.
* {{I|Lucky Foot}} / {{I|Virgo}} / {{I|PHD}}: Can help Tainted Isaac build up a large amount of stat boosts via pills without having items tied to them. Pills that were negative will revert back when the item is dropped.
** Pills stay identified when removing PHD.
* {{I|Luna}}: The stat upgrade(s) for the current floor will not be reverted when left behind.
* {{P|XX - Judgement?}}: Allows Tainted Isaac to deplete the current item pool faster (given full inventory) when an item pedestal is present.
** With {{I|Sacred Orb}} combined, powerful items can be obtained way more easily.
* {{I|Strawman}}: Tainted Isaac can give any excess items beyond his capacity to the Strawman, severely mitigating the downside of the character until the Strawman dies.
** Items like {{i|Glitched Crown}}, {{i|The Mind}}, or {{i|Goat Head}} that don't directly affect your character will provide their full benefit without taking up an inventory slot.
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|Bag of Crafting}}: Items created by it do not cycle between two options.
* {{I|Schoolbag}} + {{I|Glowing Hourglass}}: If you change your Schoolbag for another item while Glowing Hourglass is in your second active slot, Glowing Hourglass will be dropped on the ground fully charged.
* {{I|Binge Eater|dlc=r}}: The stat upgrades will disappear if it or the food items are left behind. The temporary damage up will not be reverted, but will still decrease over time as normal.
* {{i|Book of Virtues}}: Is considered a passive item by the game and will take up one of Tainted Isaac's inventory slots.
* {{I|Cambion Conception}} / {{I|Immaculate Conception}}: Familiars granted will not take up inventory slots, but will disappear if those items are left behind and will not be regained if Isaac picks them up again.
* {{I|Clicker}}: If Tainted Isaac turns into another character, whether by the Clicker or resurrection items, any cycling item pedestals seen by Tainted Isaac will remain cycling for the new character until they are collected or rerolled.
* {{I|Crooked Penny}} / {{i|Diplopia}}: Makes each copied pedestal rotate between the item that was on each pedestal at the time it was used and a random second item.
* {{i|Damocles}}: Extra item pedestals won't rotate between two items. Damocles itself will not take up an inventory slot and cannot be removed.
* {{i|False PHD}}: Dropping it will make pills effects back to normal, but pills will remain identified. Damage upgrades will disappear if it is left behind, but will remain tied to the item and can be picked back up again. This will not, however, revert back the decreased stats.
* {{i|GB Bug}}: When his inventory is full, he is able to swap it with another item from a pedestal. Every time GB Bug is picked up, the familiar will be re-summoned even if a room has not been cleared since the last re-roll. This allows Tainted Isaac to re-roll pickups indefinitely until they become chests, increasing the amount of pickups or giving items. However, the pickups may also re-roll into troll bombs, effectively removing a pickup to re-roll. This can be mitigated by having {{t|Safety Scissors}}.
* {{i|Heartbreak}}: The starting broken hearts are removed when Heartbreak is dropped however any broken hearts gained from lethal damage will persist.
* {{i|Keeper's Sack}}: The stat upgrades will disappear if it is left behind, but will remain tied to this item. If Isaac picks it up again, he will regain them. Dropping bought items will not remove the stat upgrades gained by buying them. If Isaac buys an item and it results in him dropping Keeper's Sack, he will not get any stat upgrades from buying it.
* {{i|Greed's Gullet}}: The heart containers will disappear when left behind.
* {{I|Missing No.}} can be dropped when Tainted Isaac's inventory is full, which makes it easier to get clear benefit from than other characters.  Tainted Isaac can carry from floor to floor until he rolls a useful combination of items, and then can choose to drop it so that it doesn't reroll his items on future floors.
* {{P|0 - The Fool?}}: May spawn coins and/or bombs as pedestal items such as {{I|Boom!}} or {{I|A Quarter}}, however these pedestals won't cycle between two different items.
* {{I|Rock Bottom}}: Prevents any stat from decreasing, letting the effects of picked up items linger even after discarding them. However, raising stats beyond the values reached will be more difficult after leaving the source item, and swapping away Rock Bottom resets them to Tainted Isaac's current set.
* {{i|Vengeful Spirit}}: Wisps will remain until the end of the floor if the item is left behind.

Random [[passive item]] | unlocked by = The Capricious }} '''Tainted Eden''' is a [[Characters|character]] added in [[The Binding of Isaac: Repentance]]. They are the alternate version of {{c|Eden}}. Unlike other Tainted characters, Tainted Eden has no obvious changes to their physical appearance. Tainted Eden is unlocked by reaching {{s|Home}} and using the {{I|Red Key}}, {{P|Cracked Key}}, or {{P|Soul of Cain}} to access a special room in one of the walls while playing as Eden. Like Eden, Tainted Eden starts with random stats, health, possibly some [[pickup]]s, a [[trinket]], an [[Items#Activated Collectibles|active item]], and a [[passive item]]. Every time they take non-self damage, all of their stats, items (passive and active), their trinket and their currently-held card or pill get re-rolled.

sections.Notes:
* {{dlc|nr+}} Items are guaranteed to re-roll into items from the item pool of the last generated item (i.e. If one were to enter every item-containing room without picking up the items, then entered, for example, an {{r|Angel Room}}, every item that was already spawned will reroll into angel deal items when Tainted Eden receives damage).
* {{dlc|nr+}} Entering an item-containing room without picking up the items, then spawning an item from a specific item pool (e. g. an {{ip|Angel Room|text=angel item}} by using {{i|Alabaster Box}}, or a {{ip|Shop|text=shop item}} via {{i|Keeper's Box}}, etc.) will cause every item that was already spawned to reroll into items from that item pool.
* Self-damage ({{e|Blood Donation Machine}}s, {{e|Devil Beggar}}s, {{r|Curse Room}}s, etc.) will not trigger a re-roll. Fatal damage will also not trigger a reroll.
* Tainted Eden cannot reroll {{i|The Negative}}, {{i|The Polaroid}}, {{i|Dad's Note}}, {{I|Damocles}}, {{i|Dogma}}, {{i|Key Piece 1}}, {{i|Key Piece 2}}, {{i|Knife Piece 1}}, or {{i|Knife Piece 2}}.
** Note that {{i|Missing No.}} can be re-rolled into, but can't be re-rolled out of.
** Glitched items can be re-rolled into either glitched items or normal items if Tainted Eden is not holding {{i|TMTRAINER}}. If it is holding TMTRAINER, they can re-roll into other glitched items. Glitched items not re-rolling into normal items will eventually stop being re-rolled.
* Powerful [[transformations]] such as {{tf|Guppy}} are difficult to attain, as transformations are removed if the appropriate items are re-rolled.
** However, picking up active items will also counts as transformation progress, which allows {{tf|Guppy}} and {{tf|Bookworm}} much easier to keep.
* If [[Gulp!]] pills or a {{i|Smelter}} are available, absorbing trinkets makes them permanent. If possible, they should be discarded to avoid losing them to a re-roll while looking for better trinkets.
* If Tainted Eden re-rolls while holding two trinkets (such as from {{i|Mom's Purse}} or {{i|Belly Button}}), the trinket in the second slot is dropped rather than re-rolled. The same case happens with active items and {{i|Schoolbag}}.
* Each roll is seeded. For instance, reverting a re-roll with {{i|Glowing Hourglass}} then getting hit will always give Tainted Eden their Glowing Hourglass back.
* Since Cards and Pills are re-rolled on hit, Tainted Eden should pick up {{P|0 - The Fool}} before the fight with {{E|Mom}} and drop it at the beginning of the battle, so as to not lose it if they take damage, if they intend to use it to open {{achievement|A Strange Door}}.
* Multiple copies of an item will be re-rolled into different items.
sections.Strategy:
* The re-rolls will easily remove health, but not restore it. This makes it risky to focus solely on Red Hearts or Soul Hearts, and a balanced approach is overall safer.
** There is no guarantee of consistency to Tainted Eden's health. While acquiring Soul or Black Hearts may be a good idea because they cannot be re-rolled away, there is a chance that Tainted Eden rerolls into a build with massive amounts of red health, causing the overflowing Soul health to irrevocably disappear.
** It's not a good idea to get full 12 hearts. Having 6-9 hearts and leaving some hearts on ground to take when needed is much safer.
** {{Curse|Unknown}} is also potentially dangerous if one gets hit a lot, as your health is truly unknown.
** Since both getting and losing Heart Containers easily happen, it could be a good strategy to turn temporary Heart Containers into other resources whenever possible (by making devil deals or using both {{I|Guppy's Paw}} or {{I|Potato Peeler}}).
* Gaining Heart Containers from sources other than passive items, such as Health Up pills, {{I|Converter}} or {{E|Eternal Heart}}s is beneficial, because those changes are not affected by Tainted Eden's mechanic.
** Try to remember how many heart containers are gained by these way before using them in devil deals or so.
* More than other characters, Tainted Eden benefits from quantity over quality of individual items since the items are likely to get re-rolled several times anyway. Obtaining as many passive items as possible means more items to re-roll and more chances for useful synergies.
* Getting items from more consistently positive item pools can make a big difference. In particular, {{ip|Angel Room|text=Angel Room items}} and {{ip|Planetarium|text=Planetarium items}} are high-quality on average.
** Remember to check {{R|Shop}}, as which may provide discounted items, and passive items in {{ip|Shop|text=Shop item pool}} may be re-rolled into great items like {{i|Blue Map}} or {{i|Black Candle}}, whose effects last for the current floor. {{i|Birthright}} can only be purchased in shops, it can't be obtained via a reroll.
** Passive {{ip|Secret Room|text=Secret Room items}} can offer powerful synergies, but run the risk of re-rolling into {{i|Missing No.}} and {{i|TMTRAINER}}, both of which are extremely detrimental to almost any run. To avoid ever getting the latter item, consider defeating {{e|The Beast}} last, as that's what unlocks it. However, while {{r|Secret Room}} passive items are very risky, active items are instead very useful to keep around, as they are generally powerful, and they can be re-rolled into {{I|R Key}} or {{I|Death Certificate}}.
** Active {{ip|Devil Room|text=Devil Room Items}} are also very useful to keep around, as which can be re-rolled into {{I|Damocles}} or  {{I|Guppy's Paw}}.
** Focusing heavily on Devil Room items and not relying on Red Heart Containers in the first place is a viable strategy if plentiful Soul Hearts are acquired.
* Carrying around a Trinket, even a useless one, carries the opportunity of re-rolling it into a very good one, such as {{t|Cancer}} or {{t|Cracked Crown}} and so on.
* Cards, Runes, and Pills that aren't useful at the moment but may be useful later should be left or dropped on the ground so as to not lose them if a re-roll occurs. They can always be picked up later.
* The {{r|Library}} can be powerful for Tainted Eden. If {{I|Book of Virtues}} is acquired from a Library, it cannot be re-rolled away due to how Book of Virtues is the only passive item in the {{ip|Library|text=Library item pool}}.
* Holding {{T|NO!}} when taking a hit will re-roll Tainted Eden's active item into a passive item, which may or may not be desired.
* Plenty of trinkets don't need to be held constantly to benefit from their effects, so dropping them when they aren't needed is often advisable. In particular, trinkets that affect level generation like {{T|Bloody Crown}}, {{T|Telescope Lens}} and {{T|Fragmented Card}} can be dropped in the starting room of each floor, and only returned to once ready to proceed to the next.
* After rerolling everything, check if rocks are destroyed when walking into them. Several effects grant the ability to walk into rocks to destroy them, such as {{I|Thunder Thighs}} or {{I|Leo}}.
** Also check if there are any item that helps you find and/or open {{r|Secret Room}} and {{r|Super Secret Room}}, or destroy [[Rocks]] without using bombs.
* Whenever Tainted Eden gets {{I|We Need To Go Deeper!}} or {{I|Red Key}}, try to get a {{R|Crawl Space}}/ {{R|Ultra Secret Room}} as soon as possible before they are re-rolled.

sections.Notes:
After holding down the fire button for 2 seconds, a blood clot familiar that shoots tears will spawn alongside her, starting with 15 HP when spawned and slowly decaying down to their minimum stats. Each time a blood clot is spawned, half a heart is drained, and this process can be repeated until Tainted Eve has half a heart of health remaining. Using Sumptorium will transform clots back into health, with excess clots moved to the ground next to her. Clots being transformed back into health damage enemies for 3× her current [[damage]] as they pass through them.

If every remaining clot is killed and Tainted Eve only has half a red heart left, she is granted a {{I|Whore of Babylon}}-like effect and begins to use Sumptorium as a weapon that functions similarly to {{I|Mom's Knife}}. Unlike a {{I|Mom's Knife}}, the sumptorium knife has no synergies with some items, such as {{i|C Section}}, {{i|Berserk!}}, {{I|Mom's Knife}}, {{i|Epic Fetus}}, {{i|Spirit Sword}}, or {{t|Found Soul}}. The effect lasts until Tainted Eve either gains health or summons a clot, though the effect will persist until the next room is entered. This effect can also be triggered if Tainted Eve summons a blood clot while having no others and is left with half a heart. While under this effect, any summoned blood clots will use a small Mom's Knife for the rest of the room.
sections.Strategy:
* Tainted Eve's strength is proportional to how many blood clots she has: she is required to keep them around for protection, while at the same time protecting them from harm in order to keep her offense going. Because of this, her runs can go hot and cold depending on her items and drops.
* As she is heavily geared towards turning health into familiars, an abundance of heart drops of any sort can easily grant Tainted Eve impressive room-clearing abilities. The sheer amount of blood clots will cause her to have extreme damage (due to the amount of tears being fired) and multiple "bodyguards" to block her from enemy tears.
* Tainted Eve loses a significant amount of staying power if she has low health and few clots: she will be forced to either use her horrendous base tears, or create a small number of blood clots that may end up dying anyway, which is usually the case during the start of a run.
* While Tainted Eve's passive ability causes her to drain health, the player can avoid this by "tap firing" instead of holding down the fire button. This does not affect the firing speed of Tainted Eve or her clots, and also lets her keep some backup health in her heart containers in case the player is not confident about avoiding damage.
* To make the most use of hearts, backtrack and use every remaining heart drop to create new clots once a floor is clear, and bomb objects that can potentially drop hearts, such as Blood Donation Machines.
* If you are at full health, keep in mind to pick up/use any health-restoring items like {{i|Blood Bag}} or [[Pills|Full Health pills]] after you create clots, as it will make use of any potentially wasted heals.
* Clots slowly lose health as they stay out, to the point they can be killed by a single enemy bullet. It is usually a good habit to absorb clots with {{I|Sumptorium}} to refresh their health, to prevent Tainted Eve from losing large amounts of clots later on. Be mindful that it will take a significant amount of time to rebuild her army of clots, so plan ahead.
** Tainted Eve can only reabsorb as many red clots as she has heart containers; leftover clots will remain on field without their health refreshed. If she has a massive amount of red clots, this means she runs the risk of losing any clots she is unable to reabsorb.
* Due to Tainted Eve's dependency on her clots to provide a physical wall of protection, she has a few notable weaknesses:
** Chasing enemies that deal contact damage, especially jumping ones like {{e|Trite|text=Trites}}, are some of the earliest problems she will face, as they can walk through clots or jump directly onto Tainted Eve while she is building an offensive.
** Enemies with piercing/area of effect abilities (such as enemy {{I|Brimstone}} beams or {{I|Ipecac}} shots) can instantly vaporize a large group of her clots or hit her when she is at half a heart. 
** Rooms with lots of obstacles can prove to be detrimental, as it can cause the clots to separate and make them more likely to take damage, as well as reducing Tainted Eve's damage output.
** Bullet hell enemies will slowly chip away at her clots if she is careless. Thus, endgame bosses such as {{E|Delirium}} and {{E|Hush}} will usually be her hardest challenge, since Tainted Eve will start out strong, but can become completely helpless at the end without any clots.
* As she is able to control how many hearts she possesses in her health, Tainted Eve can: 
** Easily make use of both types of {{r|Challenge Room}}s.
** "Reserve" heart drops by turning them into clots, and then heal herself back up afterwards. This can allow her to use self-harm sources such as {{r|Sacrifice Room}}, {{r|Curse Room}}, and {{e|Blood Donation Machine}} more frequently.
** Activate items that require certain amounts of health, such as {{I|Whore of Babylon}} and {{I|Empty Vessel}}, while having a backup source of health (her clots).
* [[Greed Mode]] is difficult for Tainted Eve, as she can struggle to get momentum going on the first two floors. A strong start is one with a lot of health available. You want to generate as many clots as possible, so you can quickly kill each new enemy wave as it appears. A handful of clots with a mild Damage or Tears Up starting item is worse than a mass of clots with base stats, making items like {{i|Raw Liver}} desirable in the first Silver Treasure Room. Before starting the boss waves, consider how many clots you still have. If you're only a bit low, don't be afraid to buy Red Hearts from the shop to replenish their numbers. If you're low on health, clots, and money, it may be worth activating the powerful Whore Of Babylon effect and trying to quickly kill the bosses that way. If you can survive the first two floors, and hopefully pick up some decent offensive items, then the rest of the run tends to be easier.
* It is generally not advised to collect {{E|Rotten Heart}}s as Tainted Eve, as any active Rotten clots will overwrite existing Red Health every time {{I|Sumptorium}} is used. Over time, This will cause you to lose all excess Red clots, substantially hindering your DPS potential.
* If entering the abandoned area of the mines to collect {{I|Knife Piece 2}}, then the ability to create clots will still be active, but {{I|Sumptorium}} will not be available.  If you are low on health be careful not to create clots because you won't be able to absorb them until you exit.

sections.Notes:
* Whenever Tainted Samson deals or takes damage, he will grow progressively more red. After reaching a certain point, he activates {{i|Berserk!}} and gains +0.40 [[speed]], ×0.5 then +2 [[Tears|fire rate]], +3 flat [[damage]], and will be restricted to using a jawbone melee weapon instead of his tears (similarly to {{C|The Forgotten}}'s bone club) which deals 3× his damage stat with strikes, 1.5× on thrown attacks, and reflects enemy shots when swung. The berserk state only lasts for 5 seconds at start, which is shown on a timer above his head, but one second is added every time Tainted Samson kills an enemy. Killing enemies in this state also grants speed, in increments of +0.40, as well as brief invincibility to prevent damage from exploding enemies. The effect persists between rooms. If he runs out of health while in this state, he will survive with no hearts, giving the player a short time to find more hearts before dying when the timer runs out.
* Entering the berserk state requires dealing a base total of 120 damage, and increases by 40 for every next floor. Taking damage adds 10% of the required total.
sections.Strategy:
* Tainted Samson's game-plan requires management of berserk mode. He plays like a standard character until berserk activates, which can then be used to shred through rooms of enemies. Being able to make full use of berserk is key for effective use of the character.
* Berserk's benefits are immense, as Tainted Samson gains significant boosts to his melee abilities and speed, and even allows him to survive with no hearts so long as he picks up health before berserk ends. This all comes with a significant downside: berserk forces Tainted Samson to focus on melee attacks, making his effective range very low and extremely high risk.
* Berserk is best suited for a heavily aggressive playstyle: as it runs out in five seconds, Tainted Samson should aim to enter a room, slay as many enemies as possible, and rush into the next to keep berserk up for as long as he can.
* Berserk mode's swings are capable of reflecting enemy tears. If a situation forces berserking Tainted Samson from attacking a long-distance target, this can be used as a method to attack back or avoid damage. Alternatively, having a high tear rate will allow Tainted Samson to simply generate a reflective wall between himself and the enemy.
* While the thrown melee weapon charges quite fast, it still takes precious time from berserk's five second time limit. The thrown weapon should only be used if Tainted Samson cannot reach his enemy.
* As berserk charges through damage dealt and taken, it will activate quicker if Tainted Samson has a high damage per second or constantly gets hit.
* When clearing rooms in berserk mode, it is recommended to ignore room drops until berserk ends to make the most use of its limited timer.
* Berserk mode's swing will knockback targets slightly, which can help keep chasing enemies at a safe distance.
* Like the Forgotten's bone club, range ups will affect berserk's melee range, and can be used to open distant chests or pick up items across small gaps.
* As berserk mode activates relatively easily, it can make it hard to actually use tears. Items that grant tear effects will see less effective use on Tainted Samson because of this.
* Items that grant tears up are exceptional for Tainted Samson, as berserk already grants a high tear multiplier. A high tears will result in incredibly fast swing speed, which will shred through both enemies and tears alike.
* If Berserk is active, Tainted Samson can take damage while in the temporary Lost form in Downpour II. Damage will be drawn from his health bar normally.
* Samson's melee attack can collect pickups and open chests. Opening a Mimic Chest this way deals no damage. Locked Chests still require a key to open.
sections.Interactions:
* Damage done by [[Familiar]]s, such as {{I|Sister Maggy}}, count towards getting Tainted Samson to his [[Berserk!|Berserk]] state.
* {{dlc|r}}[[Cards and Runes|Ace Cards]]: Turning enemies into [[pickup]]s doesn’t count as damaging or killing them for the sake of charging berserk mode or extending its duration.
* {{i|E. Coli}}/{{i|Flush!}}: Turning enemies into poop doesn’t count as damaging or killing them for the sake of charging berserk mode or extending its duration.
* {{I|Birthright}}: The berserk timer gains 3 seconds instead of 1 when Tainted Samson kills an enemy.
* {{I|Suplex!}}: If Tainted Samson uses Suplex! on an enemy at the end of his berserk state, it will deal extra amounts of damage and cause a  {{I|Mama Mega!}} effect.

Other berserk interactions are identical to {{C|The Forgotten}}'s bone club, and can be seen on his respective page under ''Item Interactions''.

* {{I|Mom's Knife}}: This version of the attack doesn't deflect projectiles.
* {{I|Scapular}}: If Tainted Samson takes lethal damage that triggers his Berserk state or in the middle of it, he will gain the extra Soul heart, allowing him to live if he doesn't lose it within the same room.

=== Favored items ===
* As Tainted Samson will usually find himself up close and personal, he is very likely to take contact damage. As a result, he benefits from any items that grants an effect after being hit (eg. {{I|Anemic}},{{I|Dead Bird}}), causes statuses on contact (eg. {{I|E. Coli}}, {{I|Serpent's Kiss}}), or drops items after being hit (eg. {{I|Gimpy}}, {{I|Old Bandage}}).
* Health ups are recommended for Tainted Samson due to his preference for melee combat.
* Orbiting [[familiar]]s that deal damage can be put to good use while Tainted Samson is berserking. Non-damaging ones that block shots are also useful as they can soak up stray shots.
* {{I|Blood Rights}}/{{I|Razor Blade}}: Said items can be spammed to deal massive damage or give massive damage ups in one room as long as heart drops are present to make his HP above 0 before berserk state ends.
* {{I|Candy Heart}}: Gives a small buff for each heart drop taken. Useful since Tainted Samson requires constant healing.
* {{I|Celtic Cross}}: Grants a chance for a shield every time he is hit, which gives Tainted Samson time to rush in and melee enemies.
* {{I|C Section}}: Quickly charges Berserk state with high sustained damage, and while in berserk state shoots bone-club wielding fetuses with every swing, giving you a ranged option in berserk state and even higher damage.
* {{I|The Inner Eye}}/{{I|Mutant Spider}}: Each melee swing will generate multiple melee strikes. As berserk also reduces tear delay, the tear reduction of these items is negligible during berserk.
* {{I|Kidney Stone}}: Allows Tainted Samson to flail his jawbone at horrifying speeds, shredding enemies and putting a hefty dent in bosses.
* {{I|Libra}}: Gives a hefty all stats up while in berserk. Pairs very well with {{i|Rock Bottom}}.
* {{I|The Ludovico Technique}}: Upon entering berserk state the floating tear teleports to Tainted Samson's location and follows him around, after which it can be thrown around by hitting it with the jawbone, greatly increasing in size then decreasing as it bounces around. At the end of the berserk state, the tear once again teleports to his location.
* {{I|Marbles}}: As Tainted Samson is very likely to take damage, this can be used to swallow and stack trinkets.
* {{I|The Necronomicon}}: damage and kills counts toward Berserk activation. With proper timing can be used to start Berserk and immediately enter the next room with full charge Berserk. Unless the player has {{I|4.5 Volt}}, {{I|Sharp Straw}} is a more effective option for long fights with bosses that spawn fodder mobs, the 10% extra max health damage does not appear to included in the calculations for Berserk activation.
* {{T|Sigil of Baphomet}} is exceptionally good as Tainted Samson, as killing enemies is very easy, allowing him to not have to worry as much about taking damage once activated.
* {{I|The Wafer}}: Reduces damage taken to half a heart, which lets Tainted Samson take twice the punishment from later floors.
* {{dlc|r}} {{I|Cain's Other Eye}}: during Berserk, swings the jaw in a random direction, allowing for a potential upgrade to DPS as well as protection from projectiles to the side and behind.

=== Unfavored items ===
* HP downs and Devil Deals during the early floors will significantly lower Tainted Samson's survivability, especially since he usually takes a lot of punishment from being at melee range.
* Speed downs will make it difficult to build up momentum when killing enemies, and makes it harder to escape from chasing enemies too.
* {{dlc|nr+}} {{T|Ice Cube}}/{{i|Uranus}}: While in berserk mode, killing enemies will [[Freeze]] them and will not refill berserk mode's timer.
* {{i|Taurus}}: Upon activating berserk state, Tainted Samson will likely also activate Taurus' effect, limiting him to exclusively contact damage, which can waste entire berserks if activated at inopportune times. Contact damage from Taurus also does not refill berserk mode's timer.

sections.Strategy:
* The randomness of {{C|Apollyon}}'s {{I|Void|dlc=x}} is substituted for a guaranteed DPS upgrade with {{I|Abyss|dlc=x}}. This allows for easier judgement over whether active or mediocre items should be destroyed.
** Some Items give [[Abyss#Special Locusts|Special locusts]]. However, many of these Items are quite powerful, and may be more valuable if collected than if they are turned into Locusts.
* If Tainted Apollyon uses Abyss while picking up an active item, it will be turned into a locust; this is due to the change to items being able to be destroyed while being picked up in ''Repentance''.
** This does not apply to any other characters, as Tainted Apollyon is the only one who can have Abyss in his consumable slot, and therefore both pick up an active item and use Abyss simultaneously.
** Be careful of swapping active items while picking up a new one as the old item will also be turned into a locust.
* In rooms where the player is presented a choice between several items (i.e. {{R|Boss Rush}}, {{R|Treasure Room}}s on the alternate path, {{R|Treasure Room}}s / {{R|Boss Room}}s under the effect of {{I|More Options}} / {{I|There's Options}}, certain {{R|Angel Room}} layouts, etc.) using Abyss will only give one locust for each item choice/set.
** This does not apply to rooms where the player can collect multiple items without penalty such as a {{R|Library}}, which can be fully absorbed, making them extremely useful to find.
* Locusts deal full damage per tick, meaning that it is important to find a balance between the number of locusts spawned and amount of damage dealt. Items from the [[Boss (Item Pool)|Boss item pool]] are usually good sources of damage, so it may be worth it to seek them out immediately.
** {{I|Ipecac}}, for example, generates a unique poison locust with increased damage when Abyss consumes it; however, taking the item itself is almost always a superior choice, as the damage bonus from Ipecac affects all locusts Apollyon has, scaling further than the single locust would.
*** Already having very high damage and low tears, such as through {{I|Polyphemus}}, can make it a better idea to turn it into a locust, however.
* Like {{I|Void}}, Abyss can be used while holding an item, meaning it is completely possible to buy shop items and consume the item to grant a locust. One-time or low-use items such as {{I|Mom's Coin Purse}} and {{I|Battery Pack}} can be great items to do this with, assuming [[Pills]] and [[Batteries]] aren't the priority.
** This can also be used with blind item pedestals (such as on the alternate path or with [[Curses#Curse of the Blind|Curse of the Blind]]), allowing Tainted Apollyon to use Abyss at the last second should he find the collected item to be undesirable.
* In [[Repentance Co-Op]] if Tainted Apollyon dies his red locusts will persist, following and attacking from his ghost.
===Item Interactions===
* {{I|Birthright}}: Locusts automatically aim at enemies, regardless of the direction Tainted Apollyon is firing in.
===Favored Items===
* Damage is especially important for Tainted Apollyon, as it helps both them and their locusts. Combined with the fact that Tears are much less important, items like {{I|Polyphemus}} and {{I|Eve's Mascara}} become even stronger than with most characters.
* {{t|Extension Cord}}: Every locust will generate a beam of electricity, significantly increasing the range and damage potential of Tainted Apollyon.
* {{i|Glowing Hourglass}}: Due to a bug, Glowing Hourglass can be used to duplicate locusts via Isaac teleporting to the previous room with the Glowing Hourglass and then using it again.
* {{I|Birthright}}: Effectively gives locusts homing, making them much easier to deal full damage with. Also makes focusing on dodging much easier.
** {{I|Birthright}} + [[Guppy]]: Each tick of damage dealt counts for the purposes of the Guppy transformation, generating a constant flow of blue flies.
** {{I|Birthright}} + Homing: Tainted Apollyon can aim in the general direction of the enemy and fully focus on dodging.
* {{I|Hive Mind}} and {{I|BFFS!}} both increase the damage of locusts by 25%, which is especially helpful later in the run.
** Note that they do not stack.
* {{dlc|Rep+}}{{i|Broken Shovel 1}}: Makes for a very easy Quality 4 locust, assuming you find another active item early on.
* Items like {{I|20/20}}, {{I|The Inner Eye}}, and {{I|Mutant Spider}} produce multiple high-quality locusts, granting large damage increases.
** Taking them is usually much less viable, as Tears don't usually make up as much of Tainted Apollyon's Damage. This is especially true for {{i|20/20}} due to its 0.8x damage multiplier.
* {{I|Eraser}}: Eraser locusts have a chance to erase enemies on kill, which can make the run much easier, especially if gained and taken advantage of early on.
===Disfavored Items===

sections.Strategy:
As Tainted Cain has "No Destiny", he must create his own with the Bag of Crafting. While it is tempting to place pickups like coins and health into the Bag of Crafting as soon as they are encountered, this will likely only lead to the creation of lower-quality items. Tainted Cain rewards players who use lower-valued pickups in a way that helps them obtain higher-valued ones in order to craft powerful items.
* It is strongly advised to unlock most if not all [[pickups]] prior to playing Tainted Cain. High-tier items become much harder or even impossible to craft without certain unlockable pickups, such as {{e|Bone Heart}}s.
* Many alternate ways of getting pedestal items, such as {{R|Shop}}s or {{R|Devil Room}}s, become irrelevant or outright detrimental when playing as Tainted Cain. Taking a Devil Deal only has the immediate benefit of dropping {{e|Black Heart}}s, which in general are more beneficial to find through other means, such as {{R|Curse Room}}s. As such, it is often more beneficial to skip the first Devil Room and instead potentially get free materials from a later Angel Room.
** Shop items can still be purchased by swiping them up with the Bag of Crafting, making them a consistent source of more remarkable ingredients.
* Cards (and pills) may want to be checked for their effects before having them put in the Bag of Crafting, as a few may be more beneficial to use as themselves than to use as part of a recipe.
* It may be effective to leave room rewards and pedestal item drops for a later time, then return to craft items out of the more expensive materials once more are gathered.
* Items across pits and rocks that would otherwise require resources or would be unobtainable can usually be grabbed by the Bag of Crafting's swing range.
* It is possible, with the crafting of 4x [[R Key]]s, to get every [[Completion Marks|Completion Mark]] in a single run, except the ones for [[Greed Mode]].

sections.Notes:
* The Forgotten's bone club deals 3× his damage when swung and 1.5× his damage when thrown. The melee attack deals knockback to enemies ({{Dlc|r}} and occasionally The Forgotten himself) if it hits.
** Thus, just using melee is usually better. However, it is worth to alternate between melee and ranged attacks with some builds (such as with {{i|Polyphemus}}, {{i|Mutant Spider}} or {{i|The Inner Eye}}) to maximize damage.
** {{Dlc|r}} At 30.00 [[Tears|fire rate]] or above, the melee attack is automatically performed while holding shoot key; releasing shoot key makes him immediately throw his bone club (without the usual delay).
** {{Dlc|r}} If The Forgotten's damage stat is lower than 3.5, the bone toss attack deals 1x his damage + 1.75 instead, which can be more helpful when he has low damage.
** A bone toss attack has the exact same property (base damage, triggering of [[Tear Effects|tear effects]], etc.) as the melee attack right before it.
** The Forgotten's bone club passes through walls, obstacles, and enemies. The thrown bone club can hit an enemy up to two times (once after throwing and once whilst returning).
* The Forgotten has some unique [[deal with the Devil]] mechanics:
** {{dlc|nr}} The Forgotten cannot take deals with the Devil as he only has bone hearts, but The Soul can with its soul hearts.
*** {{dlc|r}} The Forgotten can take devil deals at the cost of Bone Hearts, equally to normal Red Hearts.
**** {{dlc|r}} As such, it is possible to softlock the game by taking a deal that would kill The Forgotten and switching to The Soul.
***** {{dlc+|r}} It is possible to avoid this softlock with {{i|Birthright}}, since the Soul won't be chained to the Forgotten.{{dlc-}}
** If a deal would deal lethal damage to The Soul, quickly switching to The Forgotten will keep him alive. This can even be done to take 3-heart deals for one soul heart.
*** If The Soul has no Hearts, switching to The Soul is disabled until another Soul or Black Heart is acquired.
** Losing red hearts inside bone heart containers does not count as red heart damage for devil deal chances, but breaking bone heart containers does. ({{dlc|nr}} This includes breaking them through self-damaging items, Curse Room usage, Sacrifice Rooms, Devil Beggars, Blood Donation Machines, etc.)
* The Forgotten's melee attack can collect pickups and open chests.
** Opening a {{E|Mimic Chest}} this way deals no damage.
** {{e|Bomb Chest}}s cannot be opened this way. {{E|Locked Chest}}s and {{E|Eternal Chest}}s still require a {{e|Key}} or the {{t|Paper Clip}} to open.
** Items that can be moved but cannot be picked up are pushed. This can launch {{e|Bomb}}s {{i|Dr. Fetus}}-style or knock {{e|Troll Bomb}}s away.
* The Forgotten has +20% chance to replace a Soul Heart drop with a Bone Heart.
* The [[shot speed]] and [[tear falling speed]] stats have no effect on The Forgotten's melee attack or bone toss.
* The [[range]] stat increases how far away from The Forgotten the melee attack's arcs appear. It doesn't affect the bone toss.
** {{Dlc|r}} Range of the bone toss is very slightly affected by range stat.
* The range of the melee attack scales with character size, but if character size is smaller than initial size, the melee attack range does not become smaller than initial.
* To switch between two pills/cards, press the swap key twice quickly.
* Picking up health upgrades as The Soul will convert them into soul hearts, just like {{C|???}}. It's generally advisable to pick up health as The Forgotten, since bone hearts are much rarer.
* Bone Hearts cannot be broken if filled with at least a Half Red Heart, even if a full heart of damage is taken. This can be abused to repeatedly pay a half-red heart to step on a spike in a {{r|Sacrifice Room}}, for example.
* {{dlc|nr}} Unidentified pills are more safely consumed in Soul form, as a [[Hematemesis]] pill can be very detrimental for The Forgotten but has no negative effect when consumed as The Soul.
** {{dlc|nr}} [[Health Down]] pills are converted to [[Health Up]] for both forms, but the empty bone heart gained may be risky for retaining Devil Room chances.
*** {{dlc|r}} Health Down pills aren't converted to Health Up anymore.
* {{dlc+|r}} With {{i|Birthright}}, the player can leave The Forgotten's body in a room and move to a different room with The Soul. When the player switches control back to The Forgotten, The Soul instantly teleports back to the other room where the body was left in.{{dlc-}}
** {{dlc+|r}} This makes it possible to enter and leave {{R|Curse Room}}s entirely without taking damage - leave the body outside of the Curse Room, go into the Curse Room as The Soul, then switch control to leave.{{dlc-}}
** {{dlc+|r}} This behavior can possibly complicate things at the {{E|Rotgut}} fight if the body is brought inside Rotgut - after the player defeats the third phase of the boss as The Soul and is ejected back into the boss room, switching control back to The Forgotten will teleport the player back into the third phase of the fight, with that phase of the boss having respawned.{{dlc-}}
* {{dlc+|r}} In Co-Op mode, if The Forgotten dies, their ghost baby will wield the bone club instead of firing tears.{{dlc-}}
* For the purpose of entering Challenge rooms such as {{R|Boss Challenge Room}}s, the health of the Forgotten and The Soul are treated separately, bypassing the usual restrictions on these rooms in Repentance. This means that the player can lower the health of either The Forgotten or The Soul to a single heart to enter, and switch to the other once inside for a larger health pool.
* Broken hearts are added to the current form, and are kept there when switching.

sections.Notes:
* At the start of charging the {{i|Brimstone}} attack, Azazel will fire {{i|Hemoptysis}}, causing a short-range, high-knockback "sneeze" attack that will curse enemies hit with a small Brimstone icon that hovers above its head and deal 1.5× damage. Hitting enemies with the Hemoptysis sneeze halves Brimstone's remaining charge time. Enemies will also take damage when knocked into walls or obstacles, and deal damage when colliding with other enemies.
* Furthermore, enemies cursed by Hemoptysis will take full damage instead of half damage (and +3 flat damage after multipliers) from his Brimstone beam for approximately 5 seconds; if killed during this time with Brimstone, they will explode, dealing damage to nearby enemies and spreading the curse to them. The Brimstone curse also applies to any enemies spawned by an enemy already affected by the curse. For example, the enemies and bosses spawned by {{E|Mom's Heart}} will also have the curse if Mom's Heart had the curse at the time.
* While the Brimstone curse appears and acts as a status effect, it can be applied infinitely to Bosses and ignores their status effect immunity cooldown.
* Unlike Azazel, Tainted Azazel's wings are clipped and, as such, he doesn't start with [[Flight]].
* When Tainted Azazel dies in [[Co-op]], his ghost will maintain his Brimstone and Hemoptysis abilities. The first is weakened by the damage debuff applied to ghostly players, and the second is weakened as it has a very small size when dead.
sections.Strategy:
* Using the sneeze in tandem with Brimstone is vital to use Tainted Azazel properly. Doing so will at least make him attack twice as fast and at best cause massive damage to enemies, making the run's speed highly variable on how well the player administrates the attack.
* The sneeze can be used both defensively to push enemies away and shred them with the curse from afar and rejecting projectiles, but also pushing enemies to a wall or spikes will make them suffer high damage; the player should consider if it's better for the enemy to die right away or be pushed into enemies to pass the curse on.
* This translates into a highly offensive play style, chaining attacks started up close to enemies to charge the laser to soften enemies far away while walking closer to sneeze on them and repeat. This cycle is more evident with bosses, especially stationary ones like {{E|Gurdy}} and {{E|Hush}}.
* Failing to connect the sneeze often means having to either charge a significantly slower and weaker Brimstone shot or be unable to start the charge waiting for the sneeze to cooldown, although a short time, can leave Tainted Azazel without self-defense options without aid from bombs or familiars and missing attacking opportunities, especially with highly mobile enemies like {{E|The Pile}} and {{e|Delirium}}.

=== Favored Items ===
* {{I|2Spooky}}/{{I|Venus}}: Useful for self-protection due to Tainted Keeper's low fire rate, which makes it easier to defend against chasing enemies.
* {{I|Birthright}} strongly attracts vanishing coins, making it much easier to amass resources.
** {{T|Broken Magnet}} acts as a weaker version of Birthright, while also affecting normal non-vanishing coins.
* {{I|The Boomerang}}/{{I|Jaw Bone}} allow for Tainted Keeper to retrieve dropped coins that are otherwise inaccessible, such as ones over a pit or a gap.

* Most Penny Trinkets are powerful from the sheer amount of coins Tainted Keeper is able to earn.
** {{T|Burnt Penny}} and {{T|Flat Penny}} allow Tainted Keeper to obtain large amounts of keys and bombs.

** {{T|Charged Penny}} allows for quickly charging active items, and can serve as a pseudo-{{I|Jumper Cables}}.
** {{T|Counterfeit Penny}} can give an additional coin for each one you pick up, helping you gather money much more quickly and allowing you to afford more items.
** {{T|Rotten Penny}} allows Tainted Keeper to amass a large amount of blue flies.
*** {{T|Bloody Penny}} and {{T|Blessed Penny}} act as somewhat weaker versions of the Rotten Penny, due to Tainted Keeper replacing all heart drops with flies.
* {{I|Coupon}} works on any purchasable item.
* {{I|D7}} Because coin drops are determined by the seed, the D7 can be used to reset a room with a valuable coin to get it twice. Can additionally be used in {{R|Shop}}s and {{R|Secret Room}}s to refight {{E|Greed}} and {{E|Super Greed}}, allowing for large coin generation.

* {{T|Door Stop}} effectively allows for infinite money with enough patience. Tainted Keeper can leave 1 monster alive in a room, leave, and re-enter to collect even more coins from killing enemies. The chance of them dropping another coin lessens and lessens, so it could be uneffective.
* {{I|Fanny Pack}} can be used to break the game in a room with many enemies by taking damage and killing enemies to heal back the lost health. Fanny Pack may provide bombs when you take damage, allowing you to continuously bomb out of the room and re-enter.
* {{i|Glass Cannon}} essentially has no downside, as any hit will already leave Tainted Keeper at one coin heart by default.
* {{I|Golden Razor}} is very useful for end-game bosses since Tainted Keeper usually has a large stock of coins with few places to spend them.

Keep in mind that you do have to buy most of your things, and that lowering your coins below each threshold will also remove a coin heart.

On Tainted Keeper, petrified enemies drop 0-1 pennies instead of 1-4, but in a freshly uncleared room, this can still result in an equal loss at worst as the enemy will still drop 1 coin if killed by Tainted Keeper.

sections.Strategy: Throughout the majority of a run, Tainted Jacob is harassed by Dark Esau with no intended way of permanently getting rid of him. Because of this, playing as Tainted Jacob requires the player to manage both the playable Jacob and his vengeful brother Esau. * Using {{i|Anima Sola}} is key to success for Tainted Jacob, as it can help prevent damage from Dark Esau or turn him into a powerful weapon against enemies. * In the {{S|Mines}}, Tainted Jacob can intentionally run into Dark Esau in order to abuse the mechanics of The Lost form (specifically Flight in an area which normally removes any previous sources of flight you may have attained) to quickly and easily acquire the {{I|Knife Piece 2}} with a rapid and flight-assisted escape if you are attempting to reach the {{S|Corpse}} to defeat {{E|Mother}}. ** Typically, the escape path would become excessively difficult due to both {{E|Mother's Shadow}} and Dark Esau attempting to charge at you in intervals which are typically out of sync, making it very difficult to escape without taking damage or potentially dying. ** By remaining in The Lost form, this also allows you bypass the damage which would normally be required to enter the door in order to advance to {{S|Mausoleum}} / {{S|Gehenna}}. ** It is recommended to fully clear the floor first, as Tainted Jacob remains in The Lost form until the next floor is reached. * While in his Lost form, Tainted Jacob can take Devil Deals in the same way as the Lost. At the end of each floor with a Devil Deal spawn, it is possible to intentionally have Dark Esau turn Tainted Jacob into The Lost form in order to receive free Devil Deals. * Items and transformations that give you flight ({{tf|Guppy}}, {{tf|Beelzebub}}, {{tf|Seraphim}}, and {{tf|Leviathan}}) to be able to more easily dodge Dark Esau in rooms with pits and rocks, and/or spectral tears (quicker room clears with obstacles plus can cheese obstacle mechanics with Dark Esau) can help quickly clear rooms and avoid the brother's attacks. * {{t|Perfection}} is '''''not''''' lost upon getting hit by Dark Esau. * It can actually be quite risky to take {{i|Birthright}}. Each Dark Esau can charge in a different direction than the other, which ultimately increases your chances of getting hit by one of them. === Dark Esau === ===== Defense ===== Dark Esau himself should be respected. Being touched a single time by Dark Esau has a high chance of leading to a run's end by putting Jacob in his fragile Lost state for the remainder of a floor. * Dark Esau deals no contact damage to Jacob while chained down with Anima Sola. * Dark Esau's touch effect can be avoided while [[Temporary Buffs|shielded, invulnerable]], or otherwise immune to damage (such as with {{I|Holy Mantle}} or {{I|Gnawed Leaf}}). * Dark Esau keeps a consistent distance from Jacob, and will only charge if he is within this distance. Dark Esau will never actually be able to touch Jacob unless he starts his charge animation, charges, or Jacob runs into him. ** As such, running from and maintaining enough distance from Dark Esau will prevent him from charging. ** In some cases such as being next to an obstacle, Dark Esau will stop moving within the prop and will be unable to charge until Jacob moves away from it. ** Dark Esau will only charge at Jacob once he enters his cardinal line of sight. Dark Esau will not charge at Jacob if he is positioned diagonally from him, even if Jacob is standing still. * Dark Esau's position at all times is determined by his position relative to the general layout of the floor, meaning he persists in the same location even when Tainted Jacob moves through rooms. Entering a new room cancels Esau's charge if he was preparing one or frees him if he was bound by Anima Sola. ** Caution should be taken when moving between rooms where Dark Esau is near the doorway, as this may lead to a situation where Tainted Jacob immediately runs into Dark Esau. ** Teleporting a great distance or traveling quickly through rooms with the help of special items or a high speed stat makes it harder for Dark Esau to catch up to Jacob. ** If Dark Esau is in the process of traveling between rooms, it is possible to use Anima Sola to chain him outside of the current area Tainted Jacob is in. * As Dark Esau takes time to respawn after entering a new floor, the first few seconds on every floor can be used to explore rooms freely. * Dark Esau will not charge at Jacob if he eats a Paralysis [[Pills|Pill]]. ===== Offense ===== Considering the damage Dark Esau can deal to enemies and the fact that Anima Sola can be canceled early by using it a second time, Dark Esau can become a powerful, albeit dangerous weapon to use against enemies by positioning Tainted Jacob in ways that manipulate him into charging into enemies. This is further compounded, as his charge attack ignores [[Damage Scaling|Boss Armor]]. * Anima Sola can be used in an empty room to instantly summon Dark Esau in order to use him advantageously. ** Dark Esau's charge is able to single-handedly kill most early bosses in one or two hits. He can also be held in place with Anima Sola to bait chasing enemies, as Jacob can stand behind Dark Esau and cause them to run into him. * In [[Greed Mode]], Anima Sola will always be charged at the beginning of a new wave. This can be taken advantage of by binding Dark Esau before a new wave begins and then letting him charge into a freshly spawned enemy group or a priority enemy like a [[Monsters#Champions|champion]]. Since releasing Dark Esau manually does not consume the item charge, the item will still be available to restrict him again immediately afterwards. * Dark Esau's charge will extinguish {{e|Fire Place}}s. * Dark Esau cannot damage [[Status Effects|friendly]] enemies. * When Dark Esau charges while in [[Status Effects|fear]], he charges away from Tainted Jacob. ===== Co-Op Mode ===== * Dark Esau cannot affect other players and ignores them completely. ** {{dlc|nr+}} If multiple players are playing Tainted Jacob, then any Tainted Jacob who touches any Dark Esau will still be turned into a ghost or die. Tainted Jacob players will only be able to use Anima Sola on their own Dark Esau, and if one of the Tainted Jacobs is completely killed, both Dark Esaus will begin to target the one that is still living. ** {{dlc|nr+}} When Tainted Jacob completely dies and is turned into a small ghost baby as a Co-Op partner, Dark Esau will still follow the ghost of Tainted Jacob if no other Tainted Jacob players are in the match, allowing them to still use him as a high damage weapon to help their teammates. ** {{dlc|r+}} Dark Esau will no longer deal damage to enemies or charge at the ghost of Tainted Jacob until he is revived. * If Tainted Jacob was turned into his ghostly form by Dark Esau, then dying and being revived upon completion of the boss will have him revive as his ghostly form. ** {{dlc|nr+}} If Tainted Jacob is dead at the start of a floor, Dark Esau will still spawn, but will target one of the living players instead. Unless they are also playing Tainted Jacob, he will never hurt them outside his spawning animation. ** {{dlc|r+}} If Tainted Jacob is dead at the end of a floor, he will respawn at the start of the next floor. ===== Notes ===== * Dark Esau is considered a [[Bosses|boss]]. ** Like every other "boss", Dark Esau can be spawned with [[Debug Console|debug commands]]. However, if playing as someone other than Tainted Jacob, the player will be immune to his attacks. *** {{c|Jacob}}, even in his normal non-tainted form, is an exception. When touched by Dark Esau, he will take damage, but will not turn into a ghost. {{c|Esau}}, like most characters, is still immune to Dark Esau. * When the console command "restart 39" is loaded, the player will be spawned as a ghostly version of Tainted Jacob. The only differences is that Dark Esau never seems to spawn and that this version of Tainted Jacob has the health of {{c|The Lost}}.

sections.Notes:
* When used, Dark Arts gives Tainted Judas +1.0 speed and makes him invulnerable to damage for a short period of time. Any enemies touched while Dark Arts is active will be frozen until the effect ends, at which point they will take damage (x2.5 your damage + 3.5 flat damage). Any enemy projectiles touched while Dark Arts is active will be destroyed. At the end of the effect, a blast effect occurs. The total explosion damage dealt is proportional to the number of enemies touched, and each enemy killed or projectile destroyed grants Tainted Judas a temporary damage boost. The damage boost scales and lasts longer depending on the number of enemies killed and projectiles destroyed.

* Tainted Judas is unable to gain {{e|Red Heart|text=Red Hearts}}. Health Ups will give him {{e|Black Heart|text=Black Hearts}} instead. If he picks up a {{e|Bone Heart}}, he will be unable to fill it with red health.
sections.Strategy:
* Tainted Judas is best suited to a highly aggressive playstyle; making effective use of Dark Arts by rushing into the fray and striking as many enemies as possible, then clearing up stragglers with buffed damage. However, it shouldn't be mistaken as a purely offensive tool, as the ability to destroy projectiles gives it great defensive utility when used properly. For example, timing its activation to cross through the origin point of a nova of bullets as they spawn simultaneously removes the need to dodge and grants a massive damage boost.
** It is vital to get a feel for how long Dark Arts remains active, as being inside an enemy or hazard when it ends will typically result in damage taken.
** Dark Arts can nullify a lot of the harder puzzle rooms, as one can walk straight through spikes and shots while it's active. In addition, being able to safely enter every Curse Room grants a risk-free opportunity to build up soul/black hearts or find powerful items every floor.
** Certain enemies or bosses that rapidly fire bullets, such as {{E|Soy Creep}}s, {{E|Revenant}}s, {{E|Baby Plum}}, {{E|Hush}}, etc. are a boon for Tainted Judas; as every bullet walked through contributes to the damage bonus, these can stack up extremely quickly, and as long as the enemy/boss remains alive, this can be repeated indefinitely. This can lead to obscene amounts of damage that can potentially last through an entire run.
* Tainted Judas is extremely effective in Greed Mode, due to the quick transitions between waves allowing for repeated use of Dark Arts to continue stacking damage and getting free Curse Rooms.
** Dark Arts can also be used to ignore the damage from the button and pause the timer for free.
* {{dlc|nr+}} Pay extra attention when fighting in the proximity of pickups like cards, pills and runes, as Tainted Judas may pick them up inadvertently and use them instead of Dark Arts when trying to rush through enemies, resulting in taking damage.
