sections.Notes:
* When Tainted Magdalene's health is above 2 {{e|Red Heart}}s, she will leave red [[creep]] on the floor and will lose health at the rate of half a heart per 10 seconds. This health loss affects all types of hearts, but prioritizes red heart health. Affected hearts on the health bar are faded and slowly pulsating.
** {{e|Bone Heart}}s are drained, although empty ones will not be broken by the drain effect.
** All leaking hearts, including red ones, will protect against loss of {{r|Devil Room}}/{{r|Angel Room}} chances; only non-leaky red heart damage will impose a penalty.
** Her first two Red Heart containers as well as {{e|Rotten Heart}}s and {{e|Eternal Heart}}s are the only hearts that do not leak. When Tainted Magdalene has only {{e|Soul Heart}}s, they will continuously leak until she has half a soul heart left.

* She also receives double healing from all sources except heart pickups, and all enemies have a chance of dropping a {{e|Half Red Heart}} upon death which will flicker and disappear in 2 seconds.

* Tainted Magdalene has a distinctive melee attack which is automatically performed on enemies who make contact with her. The "hug" is a swing that functions similarly to {{C|The Forgotten}}'s Bone Club, and can synergize with any held items. Melee hits deal 6× damage and all enemies killed by the melee attack have a 100% chance of dropping a half red heart.
* The Ace cards will transform the half red hearts, which would normally flicker and disappear, into normal consumables. Using them after killing a lot of enemies with the melee ability can be a good way to get a large amount of consumables. Consumables rerolled into by {{I|D20}} or {{I|GB Bug|dlc=r}} will still flicker and disappear.
* One Rotten Heart will provide two Rotten hearts upon pickup.
* Half red hearts affected by {{P|Jera}} will not disappear. It is unknown whether this behavior is intentional or not.
sections.Strategy:
Tainted Magdalene's strength comes from having very expendable health in the early game. Her ability to regenerate {{e|Red Heart}}s from slain foes allows for simply charging into groups of enemies and killing them all with her lethal hugs. With the invincibility frames that come with taking damage, she can not only sustain but actually gain health from hugging enemies during the invincibility period. This can result in massive health gain from large groups of fragile, easily slain enemies.

These advantages come at the cost of her base damage, which is significantly lower than other characters at a permanent 0.75× multiplier. Items that increase damage should be high priority, so that she may remain effective later in the run.

As {{e|Soul Heart|Display=Soul}}/{{e|Black Heart}}s will drain just like Red Hearts do, they are generally less useful as Tainted Magdalene. This is compounded by the fact that her leaky red hearts already protect against the loss of a {{r|Devil Room}}/{{r|Angel Room}} chance.

Whilst she excels against groups of weak enemies, Tainted Magdalene suffers against high-health enemies as well as bosses that don't summon many enemies, such as {{e|Delirium}}. Unless she can find a way to sustain her health pool for the fight, she will slowly lose health until she is down to her 2 permanent red hearts.

{{curse|unknown}} can cause more trouble for Tainted Magdalene than for other characters, as knowing how much health she has is important. She stops producing red creep when she runs out of leaky red hearts, which may be a helpful indicator.

sections.Notes:
* Lilith's Incubus cannot be rerolled.
** The Incubus can be found as a separate item, and picking it up will grant Lilith another Incubus familiar.
* {{dlc|r}} The Incubus does 100% of Lilith's damage stat, while doing only 75% with other characters, except {{c|Tainted Lilith}}.
* Lilith's Incubus familiar copies whatever tears she would fire if she weren't blindfolded. Combined with the {{i|Box of Friends}}, the basic strategy for her is to simply multiply her damage. Powerful tear modifiers such as {{i|Polyphemus}} will become even more deadly if Lilith can create several Incubi.
* When shooting, keep in mind that Incubus lingers behind Lilith with a slight delay.
* Incubus has reduced tear size, which makes some items harder to use ({{i|The Ludovico Technique}}, for example).
* Due to her starter item {{i|Box of Friends}}, she strongly benefits from other [[familiar]]s and familiar enhancers like {{i|BFFS!}}.
* All battery items (such as {{i|9 Volt}}, {{i|Car Battery}}, or {{i|4.5 Volt}}) are very useful for Lilith's {{i|Box of Friends}}. This makes money and {{r|Shop}}s more valuable as Lilith.
* Activated Items recharge per-wave in {{mode|greed}} [[Greed Mode]] and {{R|Boss Rush}}, allowing Lilith to use the {{i|Box of Friends}} very often. Familiars like {{i|The Relic}} and {{i|Little C.H.A.D.}} can spawn an endless amount of health if used correctly.
** Due to this, during Greed mode, it is most effective to stay within the Arena for every wave in order to maximize the amount of familiars copied have upon reaching the boss waves.
** {{i|4.5 Volt}} replaces the per-wave charging. With only this, compared to no battery items, starting and ending fully charged, it's typically possible to use {{i|Box of Friends}} once or twice more in a full set of Greed Mode waves.
* While other activatable items may have some form of use, it is not advised to permanently trade out the {{i|Box of Friends}}. Without it, Lilith loses what is essentially her greatest strength, as {{i|Incubus}} shooting in her place is only a positive with its usage.
* Lilith's {{i|Cambion Conception}} benefits from Heart Containers, healing items, and Heart-generating items ({{i|Charm of the Vampire}}, {{i|Humbleing Bundle}}, etc.) to allow more hits taken, and self-damage sources and items are useful for activating the item's effect.
** Familiars spawned with {{i|Cambion Conception}} do not count towards [[transformation]]s nor the [[collection page]].
* If Lilith dies with an [[Death#Extra Lives|extra life item]] that changes her to a different character ({{i|Ankh}}, {{i|Lazarus' Rags}}, {{i|Judas' Shadow}}), she will lose both her blindfold and the intrinsic Incubus familiar.
** Despite this, Lilith's Incubus still counts as an actual item.
* {{dlc|rnr+}} If Lilith dies in True Co-op mode, she won't have the Incubus or the blindfold over her eyes, but her ghost will still be unable to fire tears.

sections.Notes: * {{dlc|r+}} Unlike other characters, Tainted Lazarus' {{I|Flip}} only requires 4 charges. * Correctly managing the charges of {{I|Flip}} to get items for both forms of Tainted Lazarus from {{R|Treasure Room}}s, {{R|Shop}}s, {{R|Devil Room}}s, and {{R|Angel Room}}s is very important, as grabbing every flipped item effectively doubles the power of Tainted Lazarus. * The only way to access the ghostly form of an item generated by {{I|Flip}} is by using it to switch forms. Re-entering the room with a different form of Tainted Lazarus does not flip the item pedestals. Making Tainted Lazarus switch form inside the room without using {{I|Flip}} (for example, after fighting an angel in the Angel room), does not flip the item pedestals. * Flipping between forms will effectively act as a room transition for certain items; in other words, flipping back in the same room will reset those items as if a new room had been entered. * Items that grant extra lives ({{I|Dead Cat}}, {{I|1up!}}, {{I|Lazarus' Rags}}, etc.) only affect the one who picks them up. If Dead Lazarus collects an extra life item, it can only activate when Dead Lazarus is the active character, and vice versa. * When transforming into a different character (e.g. with {{i|Clicker}}), only the current form's items will be given to the new character. * If one form of Tainted Lazarus is reduced to zero hearts while being in the transitioning phase of Flip, he will remain alive as the other form, but die as soon as he switches back. There is nothing the other form can do to prevent that death, unless you're playing co-op and being revived after a boss death; in greedier/greed mode you will be revived if another player kills the first boss wave fought, while in XL floors, it is the 2nd boss killed that allows for a player revival while you are in the T Lazarus form that is in a baby ghost familiar form, so it's recommended to plan rooms accordingly. * Quest items are counted as both characters having them. ** {{I|The Polaroid}} and {{I|The Negative}} work on both Living Tainted Lazarus and Dead Tainted Lazarus, regardless of which picked them up. ** {{i|Key Piece 1}} and {{i|Key Piece 2}} will grant their Angel Room bonus to both characters, and will combine to a whole key even if the pieces are not on the same character. ** {{i|Knife Piece 1}} and {{i|Knife Piece 2}} will combine to a whole knife usable by both characters regardless of who has which piece. ** {{i|Dogma}}'s flight and stat bonuses are applied to both characters, but healing and Holy Mantle apply only to the active character when receiving it. Since forms change after defeating Dogma, and the item is bestowed after the cutscene, this means that the form that was ''not'' active to defeat Dogma will receive the healing and mantle effect. * Temporary buffs such as {{I|Razor Blade}} disappear when you switch from one character to the other. This is especially noticeable in Greed Mode. ** However, room buffs like [[I'm Drowsy]], {{p|Era Walk}}, and {{p|XI - Strength?}} will stay in effect between flips. Any stat bonuses given are lost. * Only the character that picks up an activated item first gets the progress for related [[transformations]], so the player needs to be aware of what character needs the transformation progress. * Tainted Lazarus takes a lot of micromanagement compared to most other characters. It can be difficult to accomplish simple tasks due to the forced switching between forms and {{I|Flip}}'s long charge time. Try to stay ahead of this, and pay close attention to what form is active and when they will shift. Something such as collecting an item from a Treasure Room or Curse Room can potentially go wrong if enemies happen to be inside, as when they are defeated, Tainted Lazarus will switch form. This can lead to an undesired item on one form, or a forced use of Flip. ** If an Angel Room has an item you would prefer on one form over the other, and Flip is not currently charged, using a bomb on the Angel Statue and fighting the Angel that spawns will make Tainted Lazarus flip upon the fight's completion. This does not flip the item, however. ** {{R|Challenge Room}}s and {{R|Boss Rush}} will flip Tainted Lazarus every wave. * Active items will recharge even when the other form is active. For example, it will take 3 rooms to charge an active item that requires 3 bars to charge, despite the fact that the flipped form doesn't have the same active item. This effectively allows him to double the active item slots. * Tainted Lazarus's strength lies in his control over his health bars. Using Flip strategically can avoid death if one form is low, save a deal chance if one character only has Red Hearts. * If one form of Tainted Lazarus has flight and a room is cleared while above usually inaccessible land, Tainted Lazarus will gain a temporary flight for the current room. * Greed and Greedier Modes have the following interactions with Tainted Lazarus: ** Each completed wave swaps from one form of Tainted Lazarus to the other, which locks him in the flip animation for about a second. He cannot fire tears while in this animation. ** Temporary buffs, such as {{I|The Book of Belial}} or {{P|XI - Strength}}, will disappear when switching from one character to the other. ** Clearing the room before {{e|Ultra Greed}} does not switch characters. * Some items and trinkets with the [[Item Tags lazarussharedglobal|lazarussharedglobal item tag]] are shared between both forms. This includes items that map parts of the floor such as {{I|The Compass}}, items that increase devil/angel deal chance such as {{I|Black Candle}}, and items/trinkets that spawn new or altered rooms on each floor such as {{I|Voodoo Head}}. Items that grant a shared effect and a stat boost (such as {{I|Pentagram}}, which grants a damage increase and increases devil deal chance), will not transfer the stat increases between forms. * Items that affect [[Room Clear Awards|room clear awards]] (for example, {{i|Contract From Below}}) work only when the character holding the item appears after clearing the room. * {{I|Steam Sale}} is not shared between the two. * During {{E|Dogma}} + {{E|The Beast}} fight, flips happen between each boss, including the Ultra Harbingers. * While playing [[Repentance Co-Op|co-op]], Tainted Lazarus will still swap between forms while dead; if one of Tainted Lazarus' forms dies while the other is alive, he will alternate between being a ghost baby and a normal character. ** To be able to revive the dead version of Tainted Lazarus, the player must enter the boss fight while being on the alive form of the character, as the flip takes place BEFORE the revive process. * Clearing a room under the effects of [[Paralysis]] will keep Tainted Lazarus's current state instead of switching to his counterpart. * Items that affect item generation ({{I|Chaos}}, {{I|Sacred Orb}}, etc.) will only take effect when the character holding the item is the one that is present when an item is generated (for example if the form that does not have the item defeats the boss room, the item generated will be affected by {{I|Chaos}} because Tainted Lazarus will swap forms and then the item will be generated).

sections.Notes:
* Apollyon's strength comes from turning bad items into base stats. This can heavily reduce the need for good luck throughout the run, as runs can be completed while collecting only a few items.
* [[Item Tags quest|Quest Items]] can be absorbed for extra stats.
** As such, Apollyon can go to {{s|Downpour}} II, as {{i|Knife Piece 1}} can be absorbed if {{e|Mother}} isn't the goal of the run.
** Using Void to absorb {{i|Key Piece 1}} and {{i|Key Piece 2}} will not permanently remove them from the run. They will continue to spawn after defeating {{e|Uriel}} or {{e|Gabriel}} no matter how many times Apollyon uses Void on them, as long as he does not pick them up normally. This means that Apollyon can fight an angel in an angel room, then absorb both the Key Piece and an unwanted angel item at the same time.
* {{i|The Battery}}, {{i|Sharp Plug}}, and {{i|Charged Baby}} allow {{i|Void}} to be used twice consecutively without going into other rooms. This is helpful if the player wants to use {{i|Void}} to fight the boss and then absorb the item after defeating it after all rooms have been cleared, or when a {{r|Devil Room}} / {{r|Angel Room}} spawns after defeating the boss and Apollyon does not have {{i|Goat Head}} or {{i|Eucharist}}.
* Finding a {{R|Library}} can be very powerful as Apollyon can use {{I|Void}} to gain numerous amounts of active effects from one room.
** However, it is not recommended to absorb a few books for the following reasons:
*** {{i|The Bible}} will instantly kill Apollyon if used while fighting {{E|Satan}}. However, taking it is fine as long as the player doesn't forget they have it or aren't fighting him.
*** {{i|How to Jump}} causes a sudden movement, which can potentially throw Apollyon into an enemy or trap him behind rocks (the latter can be fixed by leaving the run and continuing).
*** {{i|Satanic Bible|r}} replaces the boss item with a Devil Deal, which could be bad if low on health. Devil deals also cannot be absorbed until they've been paid for.
*** {{i|Book of Virtues}} is treated as a passive item if absorbed by Void. It's much better to take Book of Virtues and gain the passive wisp effect over a minor stat boost.
** It's also a good idea to touch at least three books if possible before using Void, to get the free {{tf|Bookworm}} transformation.
* Note that using Void to absorb items in {{r|Boss Rush}} or {{r|Challenge Room}}s counts as taking the items and will cause waves of bosses or enemies to start spawning.
** {{dlc|r}} Absorbing passive items from a room with choice pedestals will count as absorbing only one of them.
* {{dlc+|r}} Void can be used during the 'item get' animation to absorb the held item. This allows Apollyon to absorb undesirable devil and shop items, albeit by paying their cost first. It can also be used on items formerly unidentified due to the {{cu|Blind}} (Pausing is recommended right after picking up the item to properly check what it is before absorbing it or not). {{dlc-}}
* Defeating {{e|Mega Satan}} before the purchase of Afterbirth + will not unlock Apollyon

* Just as the Holy Mantle effect from the Holy Card negates damage taken in the first place, items such as {{I|Birthright}}, {{t|Missing Poster}} and {{P|Soul of Lazarus}} will revive Tainted Lost after death. This means that items that normally take effect upon taking damage will affect Tainted Lost upon death and revival.
* Beating Delirium with {{C|The Lost}} is not required for Tainted Lost to obtain the {{P|Holy Card}}, or for Holy Cards to spawn during the run.
* As with The Lost, {{r|Devil Room}} items and {{r|Black Market}} items can be taken for free, but will be presented as a choice. Taking one item as a deal will cause the others in the room to disappear.
sections.Strategy:
With only a single {{p|Holy Card}} for defense, defensive items become just as important as offensive ones, as taking more than a single hit in the entire run may prove fatal. However, because all items not marked as "offensive" will automatically be rerolled, defensive options available are less plentiful.

* A good way to secure a powerful run is to visit as many {{r|Boss Challenge Room}}s as possible. It is possible for the player to use the alternate floors to their advantage by sticking to the second floor of each chapter. By visiting {{s|Downpour}} II / {{s|Dross}} II, the player can also get an extra boss item from the [[Mirrored World]]. This strategy comes with the added risk of having to fight more bosses, but provides the potential to snowball the player's stats and make later floors much easier to survive in.
* Be careful of any {{E|Chest|text=Chests}}, which could be a {{E|Mimic Chest}} or a {{E|Haunted Chest}}.
* [[Rocks#Skulls|Skulls]] can be a source of finding cards which in turn can be a {{P|Holy Card}}.
* Waiting before using the {{P|Holy Card}} until after the Shop has been found in case a {{I|Blank Card}} is available for sale can prove helpful.
* Be wary of taking items that automatically attack enemies in case they kill exploding enemies nearby. This includes items like {{I|120 Volt}}, {{I|Demon Baby}}, and items that spawn [[Familiar#Blue Flies|blue flies]].

sections.Notes:
* Uniquely, Eve's {{i|Whore of Babylon}} and {{i|Dead Bird}} effects activate upon having one remaining {{e|Red Heart}}, instead of half a Red Heart. Eve's 0.75x damage multiplier will also change to 1.00x while at one Red Heart.
** {{dlc|r+}} Dead Bird will remain active between rooms at a total HP of one heart or less, no matter the type of hearts remaining.
* Eve works well while low on health; using health towards sacrifices such as {{e|Devil Beggar}}s and {{e|Blood Donation Machine}}s are good ways to activate Whore of Babylon.

'''Jacob and Esau''' are a [[character]] pair added in ''[[The Binding of Isaac: Repentance]]''. They are unlocked by defeating {{E|Mother}} with any character.

'''Jacob and Esau''' are controlled as one, move at the same [[speed]], and use the same [[coins]], {{e|Bomb}}s, and {{e|Key}}s. Otherwise, they are completely independent in terms of [[Attributes|stats]], [[items]], and [[health]]. Both characters have collision and can be separated, though the "Drop" button can be held to keep Esau in place while Jacob is free to move around the room.

If either Jacob or Esau die, they both die regardless of the other character's remaining health.

sections.Notes:
* Classic controls:
** Jacob's active item and pill/card are both bound to the Item button, while Esau's are bound to the Pill/Card button.
** Hold the Drop button to switch from using active items to using pills/cards.
* {{dlc|r+}} "Better" controls:
** Items and pills/cards are bound to their normal buttons.
** Hold the Drop button to switch from using Jacob's item/card/pill to using Esau's item/card/pill.
* If one character passes through a door, both characters move to the next room. {{r|Curse Room}} door damage will only be applied to the character that moves through the door.
* With careful positioning, it is possible to take two items in rooms with multiple items that usually disappear upon collecting one (Ex: {{i|The Polaroid}} & {{i|The Negative}}). As a result, if the player can handle the increased difficulty from these optional chapter paths, {{r|Treasure Room}}s in {{s|Downpour}}, {{s|Mines}}, and {{s|Mausoleum}} (including their alternative variants) have double their normal value.
* Changes to the speed stat are only half as effective, but the stat is shared between the two characters.
* When placing a bomb, both Jacob and Esau place one, but only one bomb will be consumed. This allows each bomb to cover double the area by positioning the characters in different locations. If they are aligned properly, this also allows Jacob & Esau to open barricaded doors with only one bomb.
* {{dlc|nr+}} When Jacob and Esau sleep in a [[bed]], only the one who touched the bed will be healed.
* Jacob and Esau can carry 2 active items, [[trinkets]] and [[Cards and Runes|cards]]/[[pills]] naturally (one for each).
* Active items involved in [[Transformations]] count only for the character who touched the item first. This is most notable with books for the {{tf|Bookworm}} transformation: each character needs 3 different books. For example, if a {{R|Library}} is encountered, and there are 3 book active items, once Jacob picks up all 3 books, Esau can't get the {{tf|Bookworm}} transformation unless the pedestal is rerolled through {{I|The D6}} or other similar pedestal rolling items.
* Transforming into a new character with items like {{i|Clicker}} or {{i|Judas' Shadow}} will grant both of Jacob and Esau's collected items to the new character. All of Esau's held cards/pills/trinkets are dropped on the ground. Esau's active item disappears.
* Dice rooms with 6 pips will reroll held items of both characters regardless of whoever triggered the room. Dice rooms with 1 pip will only reroll the items of the character that triggered the room.
* {{I|Key Piece 1}}/{{I|Key Piece 2}} and {{I|Knife Piece 1}}/{{I|Knife Piece 2}} will combine regardless of whether they are split up or carried by one character.
** This does not work with {{i|Broken Shovel 1}}/{{i|Broken Shovel 2}}. {{i|Mom's Shovel}} will only form if both pieces are held by the same character.
* [[Devil deal]]s are variable for Jacob and Esau, as the prices may dynamically change based on either of them, which can make it so the other may not be able to take the deal, but can also allow the deals to be underpaid.
** Examples:
*** Jacob takes a deal that leaves him with no red hearts, the deals may change prices to accommodate for the lack of red hearts, so if the deal requires all soul hearts and Esau only has red heart containers, he will not be able to take the deal.
*** Contrarily, if one has 1 red heart container, he can pay for a 2 red heart deal with only 1 red heart, {{dlc|nr+}} or if one has 2+ red heart containers and half a soul heart he can pay for a 3 soul heart deal with only half a soul heart. The extra required hearts will not be removed from the other character.
**** {{dlc|r+}} If the character doesn't have enough {{e|Soul Heart}}s, red containers will be removed at a rate of 1 container per missing soul heart. For example, if Esau only has 1 soul heart, he will pay 2 red containers in addition to the soul heart. This is likely a bug.
* Despite flying items like {{I|Transcendence}} only affecting the one who picked it up, it's still very useful if you only focus on the brother that is NOT using it, as the flying one will never get caught on obstacles.
* For the purposes of [[Room Clear Awards]], the room drop rate depends on the total luck the 2 characters have. Meaning at base stats, they effectively start with 0 Luck for this purpose.
* Resurrection items activate in a [[:Category:Revival items|set order]], regardless of who owns which item. If the two characters each own a copy of the same resurrection item, the game prioritizes removing Jacob's item.
* If either Jacob or Esau have familiars and the other has {{T|Extension Cord}}, electricity will also arc between both characters, and between familiars and the character that didn't pick them up.
* When entering the [[Mirrored World]], only either Jacob or Esau need to be {{C|The Lost}} while the other can enter it with full health.
* The items that can be unlocked by getting certain endings as Jacob and Esau are very good for future runs (Ex: {{I|Birthright}}), so unlocking those items could be a priority as soon as Jacob and Esau are unlocked.
* Jacob & Esau inherently get an exploration boost in [[Daily Challenges]] since Esau is considered an extra player.
* The damage of a [[Blue Spider]] or a [[Blue Fly]] will depend on whichever brother made it spawn.
** For example, spawning a [[Blue Fly]] as Jacob by using {{i|Jar of Flies}} while having 2.75 [[Damage|damage]] will make it deal 5.5 (2.75*2) damage.
** For {{i|Hive Mind}}, the damage boost will only apply to whichever brother has it in his own inventory.

sections.Notes:
* {{dlc|r}} Keeper when initially unlocked is one of the game's weakest characters due to his frailty, lack of healing, and slow fire rate and speed. After unlocking the starting {{i|Wooden Nickel}}, he becomes a high-risk, high-reward character who can dominate the late game if played strategically. By beating {{E|Hush}} with him and unlocking his free third [[Coin Heart]], he can enter {{R|Curse Room}}s without needing a Health Up, and faces less risk when playing {{R|Sacrifice Room}}s.
** It is recommended that players who struggle with Keeper play in Normal Mode to obtain his key unlocks before attempting the more challenging Hard Mode.
* Keeper can be quite a tedious character to unlock, because the player needs to deposit 1000 [[Coins]] to the {{e|Greed Donation Machine}}, which takes multiple good runs and good enough luck for the donation machine to not jam/explode too early.
* {{dlc|nr}} Keeper cannot have more than 2 [[Coin Heart]]s.
* {{dlc|r}} Keeper cannot have more than 3 [[Coin Heart]]s. This cap applies even before Hush is defeated.
** The only three exceptions to this are {{i|Greed's Gullet}}, which allows him to have up to {{dlcalt|6|r=7}} Coin Hearts, and {{i|Birthright}} and {{T|Mother's Kiss}}, which allow him to have an additional Coin Heart.
*** {{dlc|r}} Greed's Gullet in combination with {{i|Deep Pockets}} can allow Keeper to reach 12 Coin Hearts at 600 coins.
**** It is possible to reach 15 Coin Hearts at 900 coins. Any Coin Heart containers past the max of 12 will appear as an additional row beneath the standard 2 rows of Coin Hearts, similar to {{c|Magdalene}}'s {{i|Birthright}}.
** Theoretically, Keeper could gain limitless Coin Hearts by generating and smelting Mother's Kiss, as each copy would grant a heart container, eventually bypassing the 12 heart container cap.
** If the effect of {{T|Mother's Kiss}} is doubled via {{I|Mom's Box}} or a {{a|Golden Trinket}}, Keeper will also receive an extra coin.
* Keeper always takes one full Coin Heart of damage, which means he cannot have half Coin Hearts.
** Effects that regenerate half a Red Heart, such as {{I|Charm of the Vampire}} or {{I|Placenta}}, regenerate a full Coin Heart for Keeper instead.
** Because Keeper can usually not have less than one full heart, items such as {{i|Whore of Babylon}} and {{i|Empty Vessel}} cannot be activated.
** {{dlc|a+nr}} The effect of {{i|Clicker}} can allow Keeper to have half Coin Hearts.
** {{dlc|r}} The effect of {{i|Clicker}} will now fill one Coin Heart if Keeper would otherwise have no health.
* The amount of blue flies created from each heart depends on the type of heart.
** {{E|Half Red Heart}}s are transformed into 1 blue fly.
** Full {{E|Red Heart}}s, {{E|Blended Heart}}s, {{E|Half Soul Heart}}s, {{E|Rotten Heart}}s, are transformed into 2 blue flies.
** Full {{E|Soul Heart}}s are transformed into 3 blue flies.
** {{E|Black Heart}}s, {{E|Double Heart}}s, {{E|Bone Heart}}s, are transformed into 4 blue flies.
** {{E|Eternal Heart}}s are transformed into 5 blue flies.
** {{dlc|nr+}} {{E|Gold Heart}}s are transformed into 6 blue flies.
* Every time Keeper uses a coin to heal himself, that coin is consumed and isn't added to his current coin amount.
** Double Pennies, Nickels, Dimes and items that give money on pickup (such as {{i|A Quarter}}, {{i|A Dollar}}, {{i|Piggy Bank}}, etc.) will give their amount minus the healed HP.
** Using a [[Lucky Penny]] to refill health will not give a coin, but will still give +1 Luck.
** {{p|2 of Diamonds}} can refill Keeper's health at the cost of 1 coin.
** {{t|Counterfeit Penny}} allows the chance for Keeper to gain the full value of a coin while healing.
* Coin Hearts are generally treated as Red Hearts, such as in {{dlc|nr|{{R|Devil Room}} / }}{{R|Angel Room}} chance, {{dlc|nr|[[Devil Deal]]s}}, {{R|Challenge Room}}s, {{R|Boss Challenge Room}}s, health-recovering items and consumables, and items such as {{i|Dark Prince's Crown}}.
** {{dlc|nr}} Taking a Devil Deal costing 2 Red Hearts will kill Keeper.
** {{dlc|r}} Getting hit will not lower the chance for a Devil Room/Angel room to appear.
* {{dlc|nr}} If Keeper doesn't have maximum Coin Heart containers, using {{p|XI - Strength}} will give Keeper an additional Coin Heart that does not disappear upon leaving the room.
* {{i|IV Bag}} only gives Keeper 0-1 coins per use (instead of 1-3).
** {{i|IV Bag}} + {{i|PHD}}: IV Bag drops 0-2 coins per use.
* {{dlc|r}} {{e|Blood Donation Machine}} aren't guaranteed to pay Keeper out with a coin.
* {{i|Piggy Bank}} only allows Keeper to drop 0-1 pennies when taking damage (instead of 1-2).
** {{Dlc|r}} Having a partner in True Co-Op mode can get around this, as the Co-Op partner will drop pennies normally (as long as they are not Keeper themselves), giving Keeper a reliable source of health (the drawback being that the partner will have normal health mechanics and therefore won't have infinite health this way).
* {{dlc|r}} {{t|Swallowed Penny}} only allows Keeper to drop 0-1 pennies when taking damage (instead of 1).
* Despite having an innate triple shot, Keeper does not start with {{i|The Inner Eye}}. Because of this, the item can still spawn.
** The Inner Eye grants {{dlcalt|6|r=4}} shots with a reduced fire rate.
* {{dlc|r}} [[Pills|Health Down pill]]s cannot spawn while playing as Keeper.
* {{Dlc|r}} When Keeper is being played in Co-op mode:
** If he dies, his ghost baby will maintain his innate triple shot.
** He will not convert hearts into flies unless he picks up a soul heart or is granted them directly by an item.
** Devil Deals will use coins for all players.
** Because he cannot pick up hearts, he will not pick up eternal hearts when dead for a free revive.
sections.Strategy:
* Changes to the Tears stat are much less effective on fire rate at or below -0.77 Tears (see [[Tears]] for the exact calculations), so Keeper will gain very little fire rate from his first 1.13 added Tears. After crossing this threshold, as he fires 3 tears at a time with no multiplicative fire rate penalty, Keeper can gain far more DPS from Tears than other characters.
** For reference, a Tears Up pill gives 0.35 tears. Assuming no other tears modifiers are taken, Keeper will gain 0.08, 0.1, and 0.12 fire rate from his first three Tears Up pills, and 0.47 from his fourth; over 50% more than his first three ''combined''.
** Items that directly increase fire rate are very desirable for Keeper.
* Due to his {{dlcalt|nr=2|r=3}} Coin Heart limit, Keeper can easily die due to fast shooting enemies. As all hearts turn into flies, Soul/Black Hearts cannot be found to protect the Keeper's health.
** {{dlc|na+}} Keeper can take a 2 heart Devil Deal by spawning in a co-op baby, taking the Devil Deal, then quickly getting rid of the co-op baby, which will leave Keeper with one Coin Heart.
** {{Dlc|nr}} Taking Devil Deals that cost 2 Red Hearts will instantly kill him.
* It is strongly recommended to defeat {{E|Isaac}} as soon as possible so that Keeper has the {{i|Wooden Nickel}}, which will vastly improve his survivability.
* Leaving a few coins on the ground when clearing a floor allows Keeper to heal himself if he takes a hit from an enemy.
* Try to bomb as many urns as possible during Chapter 1; {{t|Swallowed Penny}} can drop from urns, which is amazing as Keeper (see [[Keeper#Good Items|Good Items]]).
** Urns can also appear in an {{R|Angel Room}}, an {{R|Arcade}}, and the {{s|Cathedral}}.
* In [[Greed Mode]], as coins spawn during waves, Keeper can easily heal himself during each wave by leaving some coins on the ground, even if this will decrease the amount of coins he will be able to collect and spend in the Shop. {{dlc|a|{{E|Ultra Greed}} attacks make the player lose coins when damaged, which means that Keeper can heal himself as long as he possesses coins.}}
* {{dlcalt|{{r|Curse Rooms}} are very risky to enter as Keeper. Entering it through the door will leave the player at 1 health, meaning that if they don't find any coins there, it will end their run. Even with the {{i|Wooden Nickel}} unlocked, it's not guaranteed that they will leave the Curse Room alive.|r=With 3 Coin Hearts, entering a {{r|Curse Room}} and leaving through the door will leave the player at 1 health, meaning that if they get hit by an enemy inside the room, it will end their run. The {{i|Wooden Nickel}} does reduce this risk.}} 
** It is possible to enter the Curse Room and remain at full health. This is achieved with a coin in the room right next to the Curse Room's door, most easily achieved with {{i|Wooden Nickel}}. The player can then walk into the Curse Room doorframe to take damage, quickly pick up the coin and heal, then walk through the door into the Curse Room while their invincibility frames are still active.
* {{dlc|nr}} It is possible to take a 2 Red Heart Devil Deal by using {{t|Judas' Tongue}}, a [[Pill|Health Up pill]], or {{p|XI - Strength}} right after paying for the item. This would leave Keeper at 1 Coin Heart (empty if it was recovered using the pill, but he will not be killed), which is quite risky as he will be one hit away from death. However, if the boss item is a normally-useless Health Up, it can make even a 2 heart Devil Deal effectively free if Keeper possess a Strength Card and take the boss item after leaving the Devil Room.
* {{Dlc+|nr}} It can be useful for the player to hold onto any {{p|Joker}} cards they find, as they will probably be given an item that increases health at some point in their run; before taking it, they should use Joker to see if any 1 heart Devil Deals are available. {{dlc-}}
** {{Dlc+|nr}} Keeper's Coin Hearts count as Red Hearts for the purposes of Devil Room and Angel Room spawn chances, making Joker Cards, {{i|Goat Head}} and {{i|Eucharist}} invaluable for getting consistent Devil Rooms and Angel Rooms. {{dlc-}}
* {{dlc|nr}} Pills can be risky to take as Keeper since there are many adverse effects in the pool, which can quickly ruin a run should they happen. Picking up {{i|PHD}} is recommended before trying any pills.
** {{dlc|nr}} The [[Pill|Hematemesis Pill]] will reduce the Keeper's health, but in exchange, spawn many flies.
* {{dlc+|r}} The [[Pill|Hematemesis Pill]] will drop many coins on the floor, making it very useful for quick health regeration, and [[Pill|Health Down Pill]]s are excluded from the pill pool when playing as Keeper, making using unknown pills slightly less risky. {{dlc-}}
* Co-op babies can be used to exploit a {{e|Blood Donation Machine}} and a {{e|Devil Beggar}} because babies still spawn with a whole heart while Keeper always has a full coin; thus, the baby's health can be replenished by spawning/respawning.
** This doesn't work in [[Chapter 4]] and beyond unless Keeper has {{i|The Wafer}}.
* In fights against {{e|Hush}} and}} {{E|Mega Satan}}, bring {{p|X - Wheel of Fortune}}: they will not attack the Keeper until he gets closer to the center of the room, allowing him to spawn a lot of coins from the {{e|Slot Machine}} for healing in the middle of battle.
* The Keeper can utilize the {{R|Sacrifice Room}} much more reliably and efficiently than other characters. To do this, instead of picking up extra dropped coins, leave them all on the floor. When the player finds a sacrifice room, they can repeatedly step on the spikes for a reward, then go pick up a penny left on the floor, and repeat this process until they are satisfied with their rewards. This process is easier in ''Repentance'', as the player can start with 3 Coin Hearts rather than 2.
* Once unlocked, {{T|Rib of Greed}} is particularly useful for Keeper, since it increases the chances of coins dropping after a room clear in place of hearts. This allows for more opportunities to heal.

=== Wooden Nickel ===
After beating Cathedral with Keeper, he will start with {{i|Wooden Nickel}}, giving Keeper a source of potential free coins and health.
* It's usually a good idea to use the Wooden Nickel right after entering a room, so that the coin dropped will also work as emergency healing.
* {{i|The Battery}}, {{I|Jumper Cables}}, {{i|9 Volt}}, {{i|Charged Baby}}, and {{i|Car Battery}} help to further increase the amount of coins produced. Having {{i|Habit}} will recharge the Wooden Nickel whenever Keeper is hit, allowing him to potentially sustain himself endlessly, as long as the Wooden Nickel pays out. Having {{i|Habit}} and {{i|Car Battery}} increases chances for infinite coins.
* Sacrifice rooms can be used much more with the Wooden Nickel, as the coins gained from it can be spent on them.
* {{i|9 Volt}} can be used to farm charges infinitely in the room before the boss room or a trap room, as the doors will not automatically open after the normal amount of time. It is easiest if there are any immobile or passive enemies.

=== Shops ===
After beating {{S|Sheol}} with Keeper, he will start with {{t|Store Key}}, giving Keeper free access to Shops.

The following shop items are particularly useful for Keeper:
* {{i|Hive Mind}}: Enhances the many [[blue fly|blue flies]] Keeper will naturally produce.
* {{i|Piggy Bank}}: Drops 0-1 coins with Keeper instead of 1-2, but still provides increased survivability.
** {{dlc|r}} In Co-Op, a player not using Keeper can take the Piggy Bank instead for its full benefit and thus supply Keeper with coins when necessary.
* {{i|Mom's Box}}: Can drop {{t|Swallowed Penny}}, and makes Swallowed Penny drop 2 coins instead of one, resulting in infinite money.
** {{dlc|r}} While this no longer results in infinite money, having a Swallowed Penny that's twice as effective will drastically increase survivability.
* Any Battery type items (see [[#Wooden Nickel|above]])
* {{i|Sharp Plug}} takes only one HP on use.

sections.General Strategies:
{{main|The Lost (Strategy)}}
* One of the biggest issues of having no health is that many items become completely useless: items that only give health ups, only become effective upon taking damage, or cost health to use provide no benefit to The Lost.
** {{dlc+|r}} This is alleviated by the {{i|Eternal D6}} that The Lost starts with. Even though the Eternal D6 has a 25% chance to destroy an item instead of rerolling it, this is no loss for The Lost if the destroyed item would have been useless for it anyway.{{dlc-}}
* Trinkets and Items like {{t|Brain Worm}} that can home-in and target enemies even at a distance are invaluable early in the game, as you do not need to place yourself directly in the enemy's attack path and {{dlc|a}}The Lost's spectral tears pass through most obstacles.
* The Lost's flight and {{dlc|a}}spectral tears allows taking advantage of obstacles, trivializing certain rooms.
* Anything that grants an extra life (e.g. {{i|Dead Cat}}, {{i|1up!}}) is highly useful, allowing The Lost to retry rooms that would have otherwise ended the run.
* {{dlc|r}} Due to The Lost's ability to take 1 Devil Item for free, Devil Rooms and Angel Rooms become equally valuable, unless one is going for {{e|Mega Satan}}.

sections.Strategy:
* Tainted Lilith's special attack method is not an item and cannot be rerolled.
* Because of the special attack, Tainted Lilith starts with many perks that other characters would heavily benefit from: the launched baby has high starting damage, piercing, and the ability to attack through obstacles. However, this comes at the cost of Tainted Lilith's tears being much harder to use since it is tied to her baby, and the baby's umbilical cord gives its launching attack limited range.
* Tainted Lilith's launched baby is enough to one/two-shot most starting enemies, while the tears it fires are comparatively hard to control. It is usually best to use the baby as a makeshift melee weapon for clearing rooms unless Tainted Lilith can find some useful tear modifiers.
* When launched, Gello deals 3× damage and is capable of pushing enemies and bosses away on contact, making it handy to simply hit enemies with Gello rather than its tears. As such, a high tear rate does wonders for Tainted Lilith, as this also increases how quickly Gello can be launched from her. However, an overly high tear rate could be detrimental, as spamming the special attack causes Gello to return before it can hit any enemy.
* If the situation calls for it, Gello's tears can be used to safely attack at a distance as an extension of Tainted Lilith. However, this does not usually have use apart from very large rooms since Gello goes through obstacles.
* The hitbox of her special attack persists between rooms, meaning that launching Gello right before entering a room can potentially hit an enemy there.
* For early floors, prioritize getting speed upgrades over other stats. While Gello gives Tainted Lilith strong attacking power, it has to be relaunched each time, and her problematic base speed allows chasing enemies to easily overwhelm her. Look to get items that increase speed and avoid those that lower it further.
* During later floors, prioritize tear upgrades or range over other stats. At that point, using tears becomes a priority, since some bosses like {{e|Delirium}} are able to teleport constantly, making it hard to use Gello's launch attack on them. Tainted Lilith usually has to resort to Gello's tears to deal consistent damage to these bosses.
* Gello cannot collect pickups, but it can knock them around. This ability can be used to dislodge pickups that would normally require you to walk over spikes to get.
* In [[Repentance Co-Op]], if she dies, her familiar acts as normal, but still suffers the same penalties as other characters in this form.
* Unlike other characters, {{I|Incubus}}'s damage is not reduced by 25% while playing as Tainted Lilith. {{C|Lilith}} shares this trait.
sections.Interactions:
* {{I|Birthright}}: Familiars that normally follow Tainted Lilith will instead act like and stack on top of her {{i|Gello}} familiar, disappearing inside of her while she's not firing and swinging out when she attacks. The melee attack gains a flat +3 damage bonus per familiar (regardless of damage multipliers) and if those familiars can shoot, they do so along with the Gello familiar. The Gello familiar gains the properties of {{i|King Baby}}, causing attached familiars to automatically aim and shoot at enemies. Familiars like {{i|Jaw Bone}} or {{i|Holy Water}} still function, but they are bound to the Gello familiar rather than their normal means of movement. {{i|Lil Delirium}} is only affected by this when it transforms into an appropriate familiar.
* {{I|Box of Friends}} Does not copy Gello.
* {{I|Brimstone}}: Gello automatically charges and shoots a laser towards enemies.
* {{T|Child Leash}}: Increases the size of the Gello familiar, but does not change the length the Gello familiar is fired. {{dlc|r+}} Also does not provide the 1.25x damage multiplier to the whip attack or the familiar's shots.
* {{I|Chocolate Milk}}: Automatically charges and shoots Chocolate Milk shots towards enemies. Gello fires higher damage shots if farther from the enemy and lower damage shots if closer to the enemy.
* {{I|Cursed Eye}}: Gello gains the charge effect, but the teleport effect when damaged while charging does not happen.
* {{T|Forgotten Lullaby}}: Does not improve the fire rate of Gello.
* {{I|The Inner Eye}}: Lowers Lilith's tear rate and doesn't triple her familiar.  However, her familiar will shoot a triple shot.
* {{I|Ipecac}}: Greatly increases the launch damage of Gello. If the fire button is pressed ''very'' briefly, Gello can be launched without also firing an Ipecac tear, allowing the player to attack with high damage, with no risk of hurting themselves from the explosion.
* {{I|Lead Pencil}}: Tears are fired from Lilith every 15th launch attack.
* {{I|The Ludovico Technique}}: Spawns a Ludovico tear when Lilith launches Gello. The tear disappears when Gello returns to Lilith's belly. The tear works as normal using arrow keys, but is impossible to control precisely with mouse and not at all with the analog stick.
* {{I|Marked}}: Gello will not return to Lilith's stomach, and will try to follow where the Mark is. Gello will return when Marked is deactivated with the Drop button.
* {{i|Monstro's Lung}}: Gello charges up, and when released, shoots Monstro's Lung shots. Greatly increases delay between being able to launch the baby.
* {{I|Neptunus}}: No effect.
* {{I|Spirit Sword}}: Gello wields a sword that can be swung multiple times before returning to Lilith. If the fire button is held, the sword will deal damage once before disappearing until Gello is sent out again. The spin attack functions normally, but will immediately return Gello. The sword swing being able to collect pick-ups means that Lilith will be able to collect pick-ups and open chests from very far away.
* {{I|Stye}}: Stye-affected tears have a chance to fire from Gello, unaffected by [[luck]].

=== Good Items ===
* {{T|Baby-Bender}}: Gello's tears become homing tears.
* {{I|BFFS!}}: Increases the damage of Gello's tears, but the launch attack is unaffected.
* {{I|Dead Eye}}: While tears fired from Gello affect Dead Eye, the whip attack does not. Provided your tear rate isn't too high, you can get the maximum bonus with its tears, then only use the whip attack from then on. Quickly press-and-release the fire button to ensure that Gello doesn't fire an unwanted tear.
* {{I|Guillotine}}: Normally with Guillotine, tears originate from the rotating head, which can be difficult to aim accurately with, but with Tainted Lilith, Gello still fires from Lilith's body with the increased damage, negating the general downside from this item with other characters.
* {{I|Lost Contact}}: In addition to shielded tears, Gello's body is able to destroy projectiles, making it an incredible defensive option.
* {{i|Mom's Knife}}: Gello holds and auto-fires Mom's Knife towards enemies, although Gello no longer automatically returns into Tainted Lilith's stomach. The piercing of the knife allows it to deal damage multiple times per second, which, coupled with the knife's high base damage, make it an extremely powerful offensive option.
* {{I|Proptosis}}: The whip attack gains full benefit of the 3× damage multiplier with no downside. Gello's tears behave as expected, which means they could deal much more damage at middle-long range.
* {{I|Strange Attractor}}: Since Gello fires at a sizable distance from Lilith's body, enemies are pulled away from where they can easily hurt you and into the line of fire. The maneuverability and range also makes it easy to snag consumables through complex obstacle mazes.
* {{I|Tech X}}: Holding down the fire button will automatically charge then shoot Tech X shots towards enemies. How fast it's charged is dependent on how far Gello is from an enemy.
* {{I|Technology}}: Gello's shots instantly hit the nearest enemy, regardless of range.
** {{I|Technology}} + [[Tear Effects|Spectral Tears]]: Gello's shots are no longer able to miss as long as at least one enemy is in the room.
* {{i|Uranus}}: When Gello is launched, any enemies it kills in its trajectory will freeze and any frozen enemies the baby is launched into slide similarly to when kicked by Isaac.

=== Bad Items ===
* {{I|Epic Fetus}}: Without {{I|Incubus}} or another familiar that can fire Lilith's exact tears, the crosshair disappears whenever {{I|Gello}} retracts into the body, and the crosshair aims poorly, trying to seek enemies while also moving in the direction of the firing keys.
* {{I|Jar of Flies}}: Killing enemies with Gello's contact damage will not add a new fly to the jar. Gello's tears still work as expected.
* {{I|The Wiz}}: Gello will fire diagonal tears to either side of the enemy it is aiming at, making it miss frequently.
* {{I|Tractor Beam}}: Gello will lose the ability to both fire and move in all directions, making maneuverability harder, and a large gap will be created in between her and her Gello where it will not be firing, making her vulnerable to damage.

sections.Notes:
* Bethany's {{i|Book of Virtues}} starting item, combined with her unique soul and black heart usage, means that she is a character who sees significantly more Angel Deals than other characters.
* Since Bethany can't use soul and black hearts as a buffer, Angel and Devil Deals are much harder to get. This will usually mean beating floors without taking damage.
** Ways to allow Bethany to protect her devil deal chances include picking up an eternal, rotten, or bone heart.
** It's recommended to maintain a large amount of wisps from the Book of Virtues to keep up a barrier around Bethany, protecting her from taking damage (and thus losing out on a Deal).
* [[Devil Room#Deals with the Devil|Devil Deals]] are riskier to take – reducing the red heart count leaves Bethany more vulnerable than other characters.
* An {{R|Angel Room}} will always spawn as Bethany's first deal room due to her starting item, the Book of Virtues.
** The item also means that Bethany will continue to have a chance to spawn more Angel Rooms even if she takes a [[Devil Room|Devil Deal]] later on.
* Even though {{i|Book of Virtues}} is Bethany's signature starting item, it is not intrinsic to her and can be removed via {{R|Dice Room}}s, {{t|Butter!}}, or {{t|'M}}.
** However, this also means that Book of Virtues will not be removed when turned into a different character with items such as {{i|Lazarus' Rags}} or {{i|Ankh}}.
* Bethany's intrinsic soul charge mechanic is, while almost always seen with {{i|Book of Virtues}}, entirely separate from it. In the rare event that the book is lost, she can still spend soul charges to use whatever applicable active item she has.
* As Bethany can only ever have red heart health, {{i|The Negative}} will prove to be a more useful option overall for the +1 damage boost, if the final run target is not {{e|???}}.
